As shown by my personal ratings, I really like Vagante.
For those of you who are Roguelike lovers - Vagante is like a mix between Dark Souls, Dungeon Crawl:Stone Soup, and Rogue Legacy. If that doesn't convince you:
Controls: The controls are tight and responsive.  You'll rarelly be able to blame a death on anything except your own lack of reflexes, though there are some cases where that's not true, which I'll cover in the Difficulty section. My only gripe with the current controls is that the defaults are a bit clunky to start out with, and even after my current amount of play I've yet to master actually using all of the controls swiftly and easily. The good part, however, is that with more complex controls comes more available combinations for abilities!
Graphics/Art: I personally reaaaaaaaally love the game's art style. It's dark, it's gritty, it feels... Roguelike. Unfortunately, I like character customization, which this game offers very little of. Regardless of what you wear you always look the same - if you start out as a mage and put on full plate armour, you still look like you're just wearing your robes. In the future I hope that more options for customization are offered; The current customization is only offered via a subtle change in your character's sprite color when pressing (A) before you enter the dungeon. Other than these customization bits, the art style is excellent.
Sound: A 4 out of 10 seems a bit harsh in hindsight, but overall, I think it's warrented until they update the game to have more music. Currently there are only a couple of audio tracks - don't get me wrong - they're good audio tracks. The problem lies in the lack of variety. Each of the 'areas' has its own little ditty, which is fine, but the ditty for that area doesn't seem to change, and after long you'll be sick of the music you hear constantly on the first few levels. I'd prefer if a few more tracks were added per area. The actual sound effects are fine as-is right now, but as always, more is better, new is .... better!
Atmosphere: The atmosphere of this game is really what blows me away whenever I sit down to play it. It feels moody, lonely, and dark - a combination of feelings which led to my love for the Dark Souls series. This mostly comes down to the pixelized yet detailed art style - there simply isn't many music tracks to draw much conclusion from in this regard. I tend to play with music off because of the repetition.
Difficulty: Honestly, this game has a good balance of difficulty. While it has some pitfalls - like instakill traps (which I detest) - it largely is a game where most deaths fair and player-caused, not forced on you. A lot of the difficulty also lies on the randomly-generated loot. If you're playing a warrior and find a good sword early on and put specialty points into sword, then you're going to probably have a good run. If you're a mage and you end up getting only bows on the first floor, it's going to be tough going, but it's still possibly. My MAJOR gripe about the game is the presence of TWO different sources of instant death: Pressure-plate activated stone blocks which fall from the sky and smush you, and ground-mounted spikes which will run you through if you fall on them. These would be much better if they simply did a lot of damage instead of killing you right away- plus, some randomly generated situations can actually lead to a death you couldn't prevent, like a pressure plate spawning right under another environmental piece which renders the plate invisible.
Progression: In the game's current state, there is very little progression, which is a pet peeve of mine. The creator has, however, said there will be more cross-death progression in the future, so don't be disheartened if you prefer rewards for your hard-earned deaths.
Combat: Combat is fairly simple, while also surprisingly complex for a 2d platformer. You start out with nothing but the basic attack your class gives you (along with a spell for mages), which consumes a whole of one (two if mage) buttons to learn. As you progress, you can place points into different 'skill sticks' (I say sticks because you don't actually have branches, you just unlock one tier to the next from 3 different 'specializations' dependant on your chosen starting class) which will often start giving you different combos or methods of attack. For example, at start, a warrior can only do left/right lunges with his/her sword, but after one point invested into the Sword specialization, you can perform a downward pogo-stick strike with your sword, unique to the class.
Replayability: While you don't gain much of anything from death-to-death as of yet, the game has high replayability due to the very nature of roguelikes. Despite some lack of variety in the level generation (which will hopefully be corrected), you really will never see the same dungeon twice and it's always worth to go back and try again.
Personal Enjoyment/Overall: All in all, I really like Vagante. It holds the potential to become a platformer DCSS (One of my alltime favorite roguelikes) when it gets more content. Thus, I highly recommend it.

TL;DR - Really fun game that has a lot of potential! Early Access, but worth playing and supporting.
Lowdown - You play as cartoony triceratops equiped with jetpacks, grappling hooks, and several different armaments to knock each other off of a floating arena. You accumulate a sort of "damage" that makes you increasingly susceptible to being airborne. Think of the damage in any Super Smash Bros. game and you'll get the gist.
Honestly, even though it's in early access, the game is a blast! Features are a little sparce in the game at the moment (understandably), but it is very playable as is. My initial experience was as follows: I started up the game, adjusted some settings, went through the tutorial, and then spent the next hour or so playing the game with others with zero issues. The match system is drop-in, so you can either create a game and have people drop in at any time, or you can join someone else's match almost instantaneously. Excellent. A round of gameplay lasts under 10 minutes and is quite fast-paced.
There are currently two maps and a single game mode which is entitled "Bounty". If you KO someone, the number of their points gets added to your own pool (they don't lose their points) until someone reaches 50. If that sounds a little confusing, you'll get the idea right away once you start playing. At first, I wasn't exactly pleased with this idea of gameplay, but it actually lends itself well to some balanced matches. If you are skilled, you are going to do better and win more games without a doubt. However, there are some interesting mechanics and strategies that come into play which mean that pure aiming finesse alone won't win you the game. You'll see this after playing several rounds.
All-in-all, I'm personally excited to continue playing the game and supporting it as it grows. This style of game lends itself well to playing with friends. Even if you are by yourself, it is already enjoyable and has a ton of potential. Is it worth your time? That's for you to decide. I'd suggesting downloading it and giving it a try. It would be amazing to see this game increase in popularity and develop a solid playerbase!
Hope this little review helps. Best of wishes, and have fun!
Edit: my mistake, it isn't labelled as "early access", though it does appear as such. Should that scare you away? Nah. The game developers have already fixed a bunch of the optimization issues that people were complaining about, so ignore those reviews. This action leads one to believe that the developers will continue to work on and improve the game. Keep up the good work devs!

If you've ever been annoyed at public transport, here's one for you. See if you can do better.
Cities in motion is a simulator game where you can be the one to work out the public transport of a city. Sounds easy enough, just some bus lines here and there. A tram line on this road here, and everything is connected.
And then you give it a while, and there's 8 busses waiting for that one bus stop with a waiting line of 250 people. Clearly you didn't think that one through. But that's okay, where a normal job as public transport planner would have you fired for that, here you can try again or fix it somehow. So then you can add subway stations, boats, and helicopters, and before you know it you're covering the city and hours passed.
The interface and controls are easy to learn(If a little odd at times), and the game mechanics are easy enough as well. However, mastering the game mechanics and planning out the city public transport is much harder. You'll have to go through several attempts to figure out what goes wrong and how to fix it, and you may want to take a look at the actual public transport system in your city for ideas.
Edit: Also, it has some inaccuracies. Amsterdam does not look anything like that. And you can just build a subway tunnel under the Berlin wall. Replacing old vehicles is a pain too.
As for the technical details, it's surprisingly good. Every citizen appears to be modeled*(*I didn't count them. at least a large enough amount of them to make the cities feel alive), and you can follow them through their morning commute, shopping trips, and visits to others. And this is all supported by the game mechanics, you can set a citizen as interesting person, and the game will show you a portrait of him where he goes. (Warning: Long) In my latest case, I looked at a factory in Vienna, and found a red car driving from the top of a parking garage(Mentally following it through the roof as it drove down) next to it down to the ground floor and onto the streets. So I asked, why is this person not using the public transport system to work and back? Wilhelm Klein, factory supervisor - Drives by car from his home, connected to the public transport, to work, also connected to the public transport system. He then went shopping at a big department store, which too was connected by public transport.
After that, he went to a church far outside of Vienna, in a smaller village where I did not yet expand to. He then returned home.
I didn't have the money, but I figured I'd have to connect that place somehow when I did get money. So I went on to look around town, just watching people board the bus and go around. After a while, Wilhelm was moving again. Another day at work. This time, he wandered to the tram stop down the street and was quickly picked up by one of the passing trams. He then got out at a connection to the subway, but instead took the bus at that same subway station, and rode it all the way down to work.
A while after, he boarded the bus again and I watched him go back to the tram station for what I assumed to be the way home. But not this time. This time he went into the subway, so I look at his info screen and see his destination is a ministry building near the town center and then back home with a direct tram line. I connect the extra village with a busline, and I speed up time a bit.
When I check back on Wilhelm, he has a new job. He is hired as secretary in the ministry building he went to way back then. Perhaps he couldn't handle his supervisor job at the factory, or perhaps he never really wanted it in the first place.
But either way, Wilhelm is happy now, and he can go with a direct tram line from his home to his work, and from there, anywhere in Vienna he wants.
Mission succesfull, the citizens of Vienna can stay in motion

Hands down one of the best free games on Steam. If you enjoy visual novels, that is. In fact, the quality of Cinderella Phenomenon is higher than many games I've paid a pretty penny for.
This game is extremely well written. You can see my play time and not once did I ever tire of the story. There are also very few typos and for the amount of dialog there is, that's almost unbelievable. Music is excellent - also something I never tired of. Actually, I can't think of anything negative about Cinderella Phenomenon. Considering it's free, the only reason to not give it a try is if you're not at all interested in fairytale romances.
There are five love stories to pursue here that follow five different fairytales. All the characters are connected by the same plot but, still, each of the five paths are very different from each other. Five unique and gripping stories. You will have many choices throughout and though they don't really affect the immediate plot, they definitely have an impact on the ending. Also, just so you know, there are no half-naked women or explicit dialogs/scenes. A good love story doesn't need those.
I actually debated quite awhile about writing this review because, as good as I (sometimes) am with words, I feel I just can't do this game justice. It's that good. I laughed and cried and gasped - all many times. Each story tugged at my heart. Then, on top of an amazing game, you add in Steam achievements, gorgeous gallery pictures, and access to all musical scores. How is this game free???? The way I play games: I download, play, and then uninstall. But if I uninstall Cinderella Phenomenon, it will disappear and I'll be sad. So this game will be an exception to the rule. I know I will play it again because it's better than most books I read for my book group. :p
Please give Cinderella Phenomenon a try and resist the urge to rush through it just to 100% it. That would be depriving yourself of an amazing experience.

Sonic the Hedgehog 4 Episode 1 isn't a bad game, but it definitely could have been better. For something made to be a sequel to Sonic 3 and Knuckles (or just Sonic the Hedgehog 3, but they were meant to be one game), it really doesn't feel similar. This is the first Sonic game as far as I know to have NO MOVEMENT AFTER YOU LET GO OF A DIRECTION. The caps might have been unnecessary, sure, but seriously, the fact that Sonic keeps moving after you let go of the button has always been a big part of the controls. Without that, it almost doesn't even feel like a Sonic game. It takes getting used to. As of the time I'm writing this I've finished the game with 4 chaos emeralds and it still feels totally wrong to me.
I mentioned the chaos emeralds already, so I'll explain that now. The emeralds are in special stages, which you get to the same way you did in Sonic the Hedgehog. If you have 50 rings or more when you get to the end of a level, a giant floating ring will appear. If you're quick, you can jump in and go to a special stage. The special stages are like the ones in the original as well, except you control the whole level instead of Sonic. You have to rotate the level and let the weird physics do the rest. They're hard, though. Maybe not the first one, but after that they get very challenging, each in its own way. This would be fine if you could unlock each one to play later if you fail, but you have to go all the way through a level where you haven't already got an emerald before you can get another chance. It's stupid, it's frustrating, and it wastes your time. If it was done well, I would totally say the special stage is good replay value, but unfortunately it just isn't this time.
The music is good and a lot of the sound effects from the Genesis games are reused, for those who care. The graphics look a bit odd--maybe even sloppy, if you don't mind my boldness--but they're not bad and they work. The level design isn't very good in the beginning, and that comes back near the end. A lot of themes from Sonic 1 and 2 were reused here, which is a nice touch for people who played those.
I don't like this nearly as much as the Genesis games and Sonic CD, but it's still decent and I'm looking forward to playing more of Episode 2 (right now I've done the first level and finished Episode Metal). To be honest, I'm slightly relieved to be finished with this game. I have three emeralds left, and I'll go back for them eventually, but for now I think I'll move on to something else.

For a game that tries to recreate those genesis-style physics and controls, it sucks. But overall, SONIC 4: EPISODE I is a good game.
The game hasn't got much story, but then again neither did the original games. Each zone is made up of three acts and a boss. Nothing special there. The levels themselves are pretty much 3D rendered remakes of original Sonic levels, such as Green Hill, Casino Night and Metropolis. Nothing too special there either. But here's where SONIC 4: EPISODE I shines. It's 2D.
In my opinion, a lot of Sonic games are better in 2D. I still enjoy 3D, but most of the time they are just too boxed up, with not enough room to move. 2D levels, however, offer more paths to be placed in a smaller area, allowing exploration to become a bigger component in this game.
Final Verdict:
A great little case of faint nostalgia at a relatively cheap price. Definitely worth the money!

The game is fairly fun for a simplistic shooter. The game looks fairly decent, it plays smoothly, and the art style and gameplay go well together. The gameplay is a bit lacking, given that there are only Wave and Endless modes, no missions, no alternative graveyards(levels), and no multiplayer support (these are the biggest issues, it seems it will get old quick, and does, but its good in bursts for some time killing, if you were to add these things, replay value would skyrocket in comparison to what it is now.) The clipping of the ghosts feels kinda cheap, they can go through the ground at any point and fly right up to you, this is mostly seen on a slope where they have to compensate for your positioning, there are quite a lot of trees that are mostly off the ground, which looks stupid, the writing could really use improvement, and there is a lot of issues climbing the terrain at certain parts with too much of a slope. The game doesn't appear to have controller support either, which isn't necessarily a bad thing, but controller support is often nice for more laid back play seshes, and I think it would add to the fun with this game being fairly simplistic; it's more a game that you will want to sit back and play rather than get up close and personal with the WASD and mouse. The combinations/element type idea was good, but seems poorly executed. The ghosts only seem to have a weakness to their opposing element, but don't really seem to be immune to others, i.e. they all seem to take the same damage from all mushrooms except the type that is their weakness, it would be better to implement a sort of immunity or resistance to other elements to make it more difficult. Other that that, the game itself isn't meant to be a huge thing, I mean, C'mon, it is $3, don't go in expecting a whole lot, it is supposed to be a small game, so quit complaining about your $3 game, if you're complaining about something that cheap, you probably just want to vent, there's been plenty of times you've wasted more than $3 on something you didn't like. And for what the game is on paper, you should expect it's more of a time killer type game that you will play in shorter  bursts than most games, but it succeeds at what it is trying to be, a decently fun, 'spooky' little FPS. Now I've mostly had negative things to say about this game, but it's $3 so I'm not complaining and with some improvement, this game could become a lot better. I will get more in depth with the review once this game has some new features, but for now, if you're looking for a cheap, simple, decently fun FPS to shred some time with, this game is for you!

I think the best way to describe this game in its current state is Destiny 1 at launch. I think there's a lot of potential for Absolver. The combat is a blast, and the world is intriguing. The biggest flaw at the moment is that there just isn't enough of, well, anything. The "story" is very fast, and relatively easy to beat. In terms of PVP, the only option (as far as I know) is 1v1, which can be very fun but I'd be interested to see some 3v3s or something. The school system is pretty lame, and the utter inability to communicate is a plus and a minus.
However. This is the big caveat. I believe this game will age very well, just as Destiny did. I suspect Sloclap will, as they add content, vastly improve the game's replayability. In six months, I'm betting the amount of things to do in the game world will have increased astronomically.
Overall, I'd recommend Absolver. I think this game is fun as hell. I'd recommend, though, either waiting for a sale or waiting for it to get more content. That's when the world will start to feel real, and when the game will start to shine.

Overall, the game is absolutely amazing! Gorgeous landscapes and areas and great art style! The fighting mechanics are unique and interesting to work with as well as visually pleasing, although the game isn't perfect and there's a lot of things missing from it (In my opinion) but it's worth it for the price and considering that most games are at a way higher price point, it's worth it for sure. Also, even after all the hours i've put into it I still find it quite enjoyable and with the PvP aspect implemented into the game there are a lot of surprises and unique fight decks that players build. This game has tons of potential for growth and i'm very excited to see whats next and the general future of the game.
Some things that I think would improve the game would be more areas to explore and a more in-depth story mode about what happened in the past and the general lore of the game, which so far is really quite interesting and creative. Another thing that would be great would be great is more "end-game" content as well as a longer story mode and more bosses to defeat. Additionally, the fighting is great and all but when it comes to fighting multiple A.I. it's nearly impossible alone. The A.I. just corner you and it turns into a "bully beat down" ( pat yourself on the back if you get the reference).

I would also love to see more clothing options or maybe even a way to re-color your armor as well as a bigger variety of armor and weapons. Another issue that I have with the game is that I rarely come accross people who have hacks such as infinite stamina, infinite health, and infinite shards. This will definitely need to be addressed in the future as there will be more and more cheaters and we don't want that.Another issue i would like to mention is that the "Stagger" fighting style can be really annoying to fightl against because they strike way too quickly with the stamina bar and if they max their stamina they can block a ton of hits. Another annoying move is the spinning punch that deals way too much damage and if combined with the stamina boost it's almost unpredictable allowing them to get "cheap" hits on you.
TL;DR
It's cheap, its fun, it's entertaining and can provide hours of entertainment. What else do you want?!

But thankfully, it's only a minor part of Ballpoint Universe and you'll spend like 9/10 of time flying around and shooting enemies, which is executed fairly good. Flying controls are great and a large number of various equipment gives this game plenty of replayability. There is not much to say about the graphics: as you can see, they are beautifully-executed and look decent. Also, there are some fatal bugs that can make completing the game impossible, but if you try to stick to the plot rails, you won't encounter them.
But nonetheless, while playing I couldn't get rid of a feeling that this game lacks something. It just feels somewhat wrong, empty, unfinished. But it brought me many hours of fun anyway. Totally worth it's price.

I received this game in the most recent Humble Bundle, expecting it to almost never be played (this was one of the "extras" that I didn't care for in the deal).  I actually began playing it to get the Steam Trading Cards to sell on the market.  I didn't know what to expect since I hadn't even bothered watching the trailer before playing.
Within the first 5 mins the artsyle rubbed me the wrong way and I said to myself, "Well, I was right not to have high hopes coming into this."  After realising it wasn't just a platformer, but a side-scrolling shooter, I was taken aback.  I was also surpised at how addicting it was, wanting to grind for ink (currency) for my next gun or sword for my airship.  That 5 minutes turned into 1.5 hours with little regret :)
There are a nice variety of weapons to choose from for both weapon slots, a slot for special abilities/weapons, and another slot for defensive upgrades such as health.  Every single slot item can also be upgraded up to 3 times each.  During combat in your airship there are rewards given for acheiving bronze, silver, or gold rating dependign on how many lives you survive with from your airship mission.  When not in combat (during platforming) there are hidden "trophies" to collect throughout the game.  I'm not entirely sure of there purpose, but I'm sure it will be revealed soon enough.
TL;DR this game has a unique artsyle that will probably grow on you if it hasn't yet, addictive gameplay with a multitude of fun weaponry and upgrades to purchase, and can be quite challenging.  An underestimated gem that I found in a Humble Bundle :) 7.5/10

I've played through all the levels that there are in vagante, and its a difficult game to master, it took me half this time (30 hours) getting to the first half of the game, and every moment i played was exciting, its all about not knowing what comes next and how you'll tackle your problems, It's all very fight or flight combat, it's awkward, but you get used to it, fighting isn't really that graceful in reality anyway. Another thing that will likely end your run sooner than enemies is spiked floors and boulders that fall from the ceiling, There's even items that specifically protect you from these, This forces you to pace yourself, Either that or risk death each time you drop from a platform. I can't wait to see what could come after this 3 first set of levels. I see myself spending a lot more time in vagante, there's nothing like starting a fresh run with your favorite class.

A non-typical otome heroine in a fairy tale world who goes from Princess to peasant with a curse. She pairs up with someone else who's been cursed so they can try to help each other break their curses.
I honestly really loved this game. The characters are endearing and well-developed. I especially love the MC, Lucette. She starts out as cold and untrusting, but it's very clear that she's been conditioned this way. Lucette is nicknamed the "Ice Princess" at the start and throughout each route that persona thaws as she is given new perspective and her worldview is changed. It makes for a very believable story of personal growth.
You cannot go wrong with this game. It's free, gorgeous, funny, and heartbreaking. Every route at me tearing up at some point, and that was before I even got to the Bad Ends. (My husband actually asked me, "Why do you put yourself through this heartache??" Because the stories are SO GOOD!)

For everyone that enjoys visual/otome novels you can't really lose with this one. Bad case scenario you try, don't like it, erase it and no problem. It was free to play anyway. Worse case scenario, you don't try it and potentially miss out on a game that might have been a pleasantly surprising. So, try it.
Anyway, my take on the game:
--- Visually appealing. I have seen/played visual novels on Steam that are NOT free with "way" less appeal than the artwork of this game. Visually, I think, it competes with the bigger game titles easily.
--- Plenty of depth and story. It is not a quick game you can skim through and finish with little time and effort. I tend to enjoy reading a lot and this was a plus to me.
--- A decent amount of music backgrounds to compliment the story as you read.
--- Plenty of dialogue options and choices. I also tend to like experimenting with those details. The only thing I will mention is that some of the choices you can make do not seem like terrible choices and too many will lead you to a bad end. Just saying. I had a difficult time figuring out Karma's personality, but in hindsight, I guess some of the choices that were not "ideal" made sense after you figure out his curse and why some of the choices might not be ideal.
--- Many endings, two for each of the five main characters you pursue.
--- I really enjoyed the fairy tale curses. One thing the story plot did was keep you on your toes with the main questions. 1. What is their curse? 2. Why did they get it? 3. In what way does that particular curse affect those characters. 4. and how do they end up breaking it? The fact that I kept these questions in my mind throughout the visual novel illustrates the depth of this story.
--- The MC is not necessarily likable in the beginning, but she is not (by any means) a flat character because overtime she grows and changes.
--- You may not like all the male characters. I didn't. I found it difficult to like Karma whatsoever simply because I could not shake the "girly" image from my mind after all that. I guess it makes sense after the fact as to why he dresses like a girl. I get it. BUT STILL. He was also a bit too arrogant for me.
--- I am going to go out on a limb here and say
is the main male character. Why? Major spoilers ahead...
I would recommend to do this route last. I also happened to have liked his route the most.
--- I don't know. What I didn't like about this game? I did not care for Karma or Grumple and although I laughed a few times in both, I just didn't care for them a whole lot. The others were okay to play. I happen to like that broom character. It is a shame they only made it poke its character out from the corner of the screen once, but meh. There is such a thing as overdoing it. There were also other characters that brought life to the story and helped set the atmosphere well. I just do not feel like going into detail. Oh yeah. Varg's name is terrible. And also,
--- There is zero voice audio. I technically don't mind a WHOLE lot. It is a nice extra feature, but I am a reader foremost and as long as it is a good story, audio takes second place. (Damn after playing a bunch of visual novels I do really like Japanese.) Oh well =D

Intergalactic Bubbles is a casual puzzle game, where you have to match the same color balls to clear out a board of bubbles.
It's as simple as it sounds and for the price which is a single euro this is actually quite a steal, cause to clear out all 250 levels it will take you around 14 hours and not to mention how much time it would take to a 100% which would mean that you would have to get three stars each level, which would make this game a 30+ hour game.
A single euro game and a lot of play value, that sounds like a good deal right, so why am I giving it a bad score ? Well that's for the simple reason, this game is bland.
Now you might say what did you expect ? Well I expected some variety through all the galaxies (50 levels for one galaxy btw). After each galaxy you get a new color ball which pops up on the board, but this doesn't really spice up the gameplay and after a few hours it gets incredibly boring.
This game does have powerups which spice up the gameplay a bit, but two out of the three powerups are completely useless. The Rocket let's you switch fire a ball in the middle of the board, a rainbow ball which takes out a small cluster of all color balls and a bomb which is the only powerup you will need which takes out a massive chunk of of the board the more you level it up making it very useful in later parts of the game.
In the end, I had a bit of fun with this game, I found it too boring. For people that might come along and ask well then just play it on the side, that's exactly what I did and I still got sick of it. I won't argue with the play value you get, but I still think there are way better casual puzzles game that are free in the form of flash games.
Final Rating:
5/10
Pros:
+ Fun..
Cons:
-... but not for long
-Most of the powerups are useless

The game runs and old version of Source from about 2006, meaning you could run it on an old PC (or even a toaster if you tried hard enough) and still get at least 30fps out of it depending on your graphics settings. Summary:
I want to recommend this game, I really do, but I won't because it'll not provide enjoyment for those who purchase it at this time. For those of you looking for a 3D Fighting game with stellar balance and enjoyable mechanics, you've come to the right place, except for one exception to that anyway.
The Story:
You are a prospect from some distant land who has trained to a point where an ambiguous organization offers you a mask which will take you on a journey to a place of miracles. There isn't much else but there's pleanty of lore for you to read and piece together yourself. I actually quite liked the story.
The Music:
Excellent in all regards. Each track fits the area and the situation, often a somber tune as you fight many foes on your way to enlightenment.
The Gameplay:
There are a large multitude of attacks to master, each one falling into five categories. You have your standard attacks, with no special attributes other than dealing damage, your dodge attacks which will dodge in one of four directions, you have charge attacks wich can absorb one hit before getting flinched, you have interrupt attacks which will stop charge attacks and have great range but are low damage and slower, and you have guard break attacks wich deal large damage and extra damage against blocks. Slower attacks in general deal more damage against guards than faster attacks, so spamming is discouraged. When attacking you can time your attack to attack faster, hit harder, and consume less stamina. You can also faint attacks, canceling your previous attack and disabling the timed attack. There are four styles: Khalt, Forsaken, Windfall, and Stagger. Khalt style allows you to ignore the flinch of an attack and restores stamina if you time it correctly. Windfall allows you to dodge enemy attacks in four directions which will restore stamina and drain the enemy's stamina. And Stagger style allows you to dodge and attack at the same time, albeit with low damage. All in all, fairly balanced these styles. And then there is the counter-intuitive implementation of Forsaken style. Forsaken style allows you to parry attacks, that is to completely block an attack and stun an enemy allowing you to counter with a majority of the moves in the game, if you miss the parry you can dodge backwards to nullify any possibility of being punished, and stays out long enough that if you parry before an attack is thrown, it'll hit the parry. This allows people using Forsaken to simply make it a long battle of attrition only parrying slow moves and constantly blocking otherwise. Since there is no round timer Forsaken players can do this for an infinite amount of time, while matches otherwise with nobody using forsaken take about three minutes.
The Netcode:
It's surprisingly good, although on occasion you may have a bit of lag, that is very much in the minority of your experiences. And the devs are actively developing the netcode aswell.
Conclusion:
It's an incredibly enjoyable game, until you get to rank of greater than 60, where nearly every fight is the Forsaken battle of attrition since everyone who isn't garbage knows how to parry all of the moves on either prediction or reaction. Although when none of the combatants are using Forsaken is where this game shines, then it's a fast paced battle of skill and memorization of your opponent's deck and mastery of your own deck.
Reminder:
Surprisingly enough this is my opinion, don't stop yourself from looking up gameplay. However if you do decide to purchase the game please read some of the discussions discussing Forsaken first.

Total War has become so expansive with so many entries that I'm not going to waste time recapping what it is or how it's differnt than other strategy games, rather I'll just compare it to other Total War entries.  If you are Total War veteran, skip to the final conclusion at the end.
On a scale of good to bad, this game falls pretty solidly in the middle of the Total War franchise.  It's by no means the masterpiece that the first Rome game was, but Empire offers such an expansive and all encompassing world that it manages to stand out from other titles in the series.
Empire is all about Width over depth.  There isn't anything particularly deep and the boundaries are met rather quickly, but on the whole that feels okay because rather than just focusing on some smaller world map like the Medditerranian or Japan, you have almost the entire world at your finger tips.
A lot of changes while somewhat shallow, are at least interesting additions such as the way your territories build and max out with hotspots.
For someone who is a fan of the series, this is a solid game to check out and worth your time.  If you are new, it's a fine game but there are better Total War games to start with.

This free to play otome visual novel from Dicesuki feature a female protagonist Lucette Riella Britton, the crown princess to the throne of Angielle, a kingdom ruled by her father King Genaro Britton III which was recovering after a Great War between fairies, humans and witches where the balance between light and darkness was disrupted and Fairytale Curses were frequently applied by witches on people. Bitter and detached from years of neglect by her father and from her mother's constant warnings to her to avoid people, Lucette has a reputation for being the Ice Princess where most people she saw avoided her and feared her for unknown reasons. Despite attempts by King Genaro, stepmother Ophelia Widdensov and stepsister Emelaigne Widdensov to get closer to Lucette and convince Lucette to open up to them, Lucette remained distant to them. One day, one of the dolls Lucette has turned into a witch Delora who applied a Cinderella curse where Lucette is reduced to a peasant girl and her father and the guards at the palace somehow failed to recognize her.
With nowhere to go, Lucette ended up at the Marchen Tavern, where all people who were cursed go to and can try to find some way to undo their curse. At the tavern, Lucette is introduced to the fairy Parfait and Delora who told Lucette that the only way to break her curse was to complete 3 good deeds where her glass shoe necklace will eventually form a pair of glass shoes. At the tavern, Lucette is introduced to four people with a Fairytale Curse: Miss Karma/Klaude A.R.M. Almonte, a cross-dressing lost prince from the neighbouring kingdom of Brugantia with the Beauty and the Beast curse, Waltz Creswell, a street performer with the Neverland curse, Lucette's stepbrother Rod Widdensov with the Mermaid curse and Rumpel/Chevalier Du Mont a bespectacled man with a blank notebook and no memory of his name or past with the Rumpelstiltskin curse along with Annice Willowe, a former maid at the palace, Julien Valiente and Garlan Belrott, former knights at the Order of Caldira who help out at the Marchen and are non-cursed as additional supporting characters.
At the advice of Parfait and Delora, Lucette decides to partner with Karma, Rumpel or Rod to undo her curse and also help to undo her partner's curse over 10 chapters which can lead to a good or bad ending. Upon reaching a good ending, the title screen will have the character's portrait replacing a different coloured crystal icon.
The game has plenty of save slots to allow different gameplay and dialogue choices to be made during the game, with a red/purple/green/grey crystal popup icon to help players reach the good/bad endings of each route and the option to skip and fast-forward any part of the game. Each route requires approximately 2-3 hours to finish. Soundtracks, CGs and overall game presentation are great. Highly recommended as a free to play game.

Great game for Warhammer fans.  Looks beautiful and is fun to play.

First off, the game system is more akin to Valkyria Chronicles, where you control individual units in real time in between turns. It's not so much XCom.
Second, reviews about brutal RNG and the pointlessness of advancement because AI always matches you are only partially correct. The game has a Roguelike Veteran system that levels up along with your warband. It will make contacts and get small bonuses, so that even as your Warbands scrub one after the other, the next one will start with better stocked shops and get other small bonuses.
Also, while the game will match stat point increases into your Warband pretty much point for point, it doesn't (seem to) take equipment into account. Well equipped soldiers can start to slowly start to seem more powerful than the competition.
Finally, missions come in Normal, Hard, and Brutal difficulty, and there are few enough deadlines that it's feasible to simply skip days when there aren't any "easy" missions available.

Most of the reviews done by people have bias... I've put about 220+ hours into this game. Without a doubt it has it's flaws and perks. But for the most part people who would enjoy a solid tactical high stake team based tactical RPG, this one is worthy of a purchase. My bias is that I love the Warhammer world (40K-Fantasy), and honestly if you enjoy maiming rat ogres and mutants I think you’d appreciate it too.
Pros
- Every match is different (after about the 200 hour mark I felt like I had pretty much saw what the game had to offer).
- large unit variety, there are probably thousands of different combinations to choose from within each warband… there are 6 total (including dlc’s announced so far)
- Tons of loot and equipment variation
- Different tactics in taking out your enemy… do you want to fight the enemy out in the open, or   would you rather sneak around and stab them in the♥♥♥♥♥♥
- Interesting lore behind characters that add to RP values. I have a warband that is full of mishap war veterans, homeless mordheimers, and nut jobs... Dirty Dan is the master of man.
- If you appreciate slow and meaningful plays (similar to that of chess or blood bowl) then you’ll get a kick out of this game.
- Runs smooth, I have a dated computer and I’ve never had trouble running it well.
Cons
*Disclaimer* This is a budget game, and in certain ways it shows its face… be warned those of you who care about such things.
- Graphics are dated (although the art is pretty satisfying)
- There are still some annoying bugs in the game
- Gameplay can get repetitive due to small number of game modes
- Online play is pretty much non existent in a practical sense, I’ve had this game for a year now and I haven’t ever been able to play an online match (There are is a small community of hardcore guys who play online)
Chances are if you know about this game/are interested in this game, you probably own it already. For those of you who don’t and are on a thread, these are the main selling points that I have found. Is the game sketchy, a bit. But does it redeem the sketchiness through awesome hardcore ghetto street fighting… ♥♥♥♥ yeah. I’d recommend it to any strategy lover, or anyone who likes a 16th century gang fight simulator.

I don't know what this is, but it is not a Sonic game.  While it may look like a Sonic game, and sound a bit like a Sonic game, it fundamentally lacks the core components that made the original Genesis-era Sonic games so good: tight, responsive controls, and blazing fast speed.  Sonic 4 lacks both.
Controlling Sonic feels sluggish and muted, like he's stuck in molasses.  That's an apt description for the game's speed, too, because even at Sonic's utter fastest you feel like you're barely poking along, the blurring legs of his full-out sprint matching in no way the pathetically slow rate at which the scenery moves.  Not only that, but Sonic retains almost no momentum, slowing down rapidly the moment you take your fingers from the controls.  At first I thought this had all been done to make it easier to see upcoming hazards - a problem in earlier Sonic titles - but the game's zoomed in, over-large view of its new scaled-up art means you get an even smaller view of the world around you than in previous titles, not more.  It makes the whole thing feel claustrophobic, slow, and frankly un-Sonic-like.
I can't recommend this game.  It's one of the most disappointing Sonic titles I've ever played.

This was part of the "Sonic Everywhere" Bundle, which was gifted to me, and I decided to see if this was as bad on the PC as the demo was on PS3/360. The answer is yes, and here's why:'
*EDIT* The listed "7 hours played" is incorrect. I forgot to close the game when I ran errands, and should actually be ~1hr. This included all acts, the final zone boss, and completion of 2 special stages.
-Terrible physics/sense of speed. You are sometimes (often) able to stop halfway up a vertical incline, run up said inclines from a dead stop, coming to a dead stop mid-air if you stop pressing forward, going into the "ball" mode slowing you down, boost pads have a set speed that will slow you down if passing through them.
-Poorly thought-out level design. One example is the Casino zone has a section where you are required to shoot yourself out of a cannon, onto a field of rotating platforms (which are off-screen and you cannot see) that are constantly changing from being solid to death traps.
-Clipping/collision issues with enemies/objects. It happens irregularly, but I have had Sonic drop BEHIND the spring-pads, get pushed away from Bosses into the instant-death gimmick of that fight (Hidden Temple boss inparticularly).
-Unreliable "lock-on" mechanic.
-Sonic's 'walk to run' animation is about 60% unfinished, and has you walking up until the very last second your "run" turns into a "super run".
-*EDIT*The special stages are garbage.
One positive of note (which isn't without problems either):
+The background & level graphics are higher quality & mesh together better than the 360/PS3 versions, where it was obvious most of the assets are 2d. The background elements of the "Mad Gear" levels are the exception, as much of the fore-ground/interactable objects are indistinguishable from background ones (the gears you run on, for example).
Play the demo (if there even is one on Steam, I don't actually know) if you actually get the itch to play this. This is a terrible game, and I can't imagine Episode 2 is any better.

What to say about Fortress Forever. There's a lot to be said, so grab a beverage, and settle in for a decent read.
Fortress Forever was born from both QWTF and TFC, those are it's roots. While TF2 may appeal to many, I found it lacking in what made the previous games great. That's not a shot at TF2, it's just not my thing. Fortress Forever, when I discovered it in 2007, was something I wanted to be a part of. I joined the forums, and the game was a very closed Beta. The community was given little tid-bits of information, some screenshots, concept pictures, and some hints as to what the game would become. Over time, I ended up in that closed Beta, and even made forum moderator.
It is with great pleasure that I can say I had a hand in making Fortress Forever what it is today. While I did no coding, I did offer up suggestions(as did many in the Beta), and some were viewed well enough to make it into the game. We playtested every map vigorously before anything was ever finalized.
Is Fortress Forever perfect? No. Then again, no game ever is. What it is, however, is a game that holds true to it's roots of Team based, Class driven gameplay. TFC was such a versatile game, that new modes of gameplay were added. Escape maps, fun maps, deathmatch maps, CTF maps, Invade/Defend, Attack/Defend, Contol Points, you name it. All of those have been recreated in Fortress Forever.
Due to mechanics in the game engine, some natural changes had to be made. Just as there were changes when QWTF was coded into TFC. So it is with FF. I have no doubt that If you enjoy fast-paced, team based gameplay, you will enjoy Fortress Forever. The pace is fast, the action constant, and the fun aplenty.
Am I biased? Perhapse. But I loved TFC when it came out, and I still love it to this day. The same passion I have for Team Fortress Classic, is held for Fortress Forever. They are different, but the same in their core gameplay.

(Bare in mind that I played this game on both the Xbox One *and* the PC so there will be a few comparisons here and there, if that's fine~)
"Max: The Curse of Brotherhood", in a sense, made me feel like I was a kid again. Something about the art style, how high-action a lot of the platforming can be and the atmosphere made me feel like I was playing something I did way back when, except with *muuuch* better graphics than what I had back then and intriguing puzzle elements. This isn't the first time I played this though as I first played it on the Xbox One, so how does this port stack up?
Well, so long as you put the graphics on the right settings so that they're not too laggy and not too steep into "good god, I didn't even know 3D-rendered games to pixelate like that before!" mode, it's fine! The controls still work fine and the game retains the addictive, snappy gameplay that helped make it so fun on the Xone, though while the graphics are still definitely nice and compliments the art style fine, it's not as fluid and smooth as it is on the Xone.
And while it isn't massively important, I'm slightly disappointed that even with the nature of the game revolving around using a "magic marker" to destroy or pull out objects to your advantage, they didn't add tablet support for the PC version. Surely, even as a novelty, it would of been a fun opportunity to have a marker control by...y'know, a pen! Oh well~
Bottom line, this is a fun game and I do recommend it to those who like their games with a cartoonier art style and for those who enjoy puzzle-platformers. HOWEVER, if you're not too fussy on graphical performance, then feel free to get it on Steam. But if you wanna make sure the graphics are at their best, then either get it for the Xone or...make sure your PC's just a teensy bit better with graphical performances first.

This game for me was quite a hit back in the 2009, it was something completely different then Rise of nations, Age of empire and Command and Conquer.
The good things about this game:
I really enjoyed both the Land and naval battles, instead of simply A-moving to destroy an enemy.
Unit management requires micromanagement to some degree.
Easy to learn, not so hard to master.
Now some bad things:
Honestly, there’s a lot wrong with this game.
Unit pathing is wierd, soldiers tend to get stuck in area’s with walls and buildings when clustered close together.
If you order a unit to form a line to engage the enemy, every men in that unit needs to get into position before they can fire, if 1 out of 160 men tumbles and falls, the entire unit will wait for him to get up, get into position before engaging the enemy, losing valuable soldiers and time which the unit could just engage without waiting for this slow go soldier.
Same goes with reloading when a unit can perform Fire by Rank, they will wait until every single soldier in that rank is reloaded before that rank opens fire.
Close range combat is really wierd, this game features some kind of animations for soldiers when fighting fist to fist, bayonet to sword, they somewhat tend to wait in line to get such animation in order to kill or get killed by an enemy.
The battle AI isn’t that smart in this game, it tend to break formation and just march into your line of fire instead of flanking your line.
The worst part is the Campaign itself.
Army, fleet and agent pathing seems decent, but tends to get randomly blocked by movement from other nation army’s, fleets or agents.
E.G, an army cannot cross a bridge if there’s an agent on it.
Diplomacy is even worse, late in the game, no nation will accept your offers if it isn’t like 90% in their favour.
E.G, an nation will not accept trade agreements if that nation is hostile to you, even if you offer them 10k Gold.
Another one: if you offer an nation hostile to you 20 different kinds of tech for just 1 of theirs, they will probably not accept the Deal.
Even nations that are very friendly tend not to accept offers that’s 60% in their favour.
You want trade agreements? That will cost you 2.7k gold.
You want peace with a certain Nation, that will cost you 3 of your best regions.
Even worse, all minor nations tend to declare war on you within 2 turns if your borders hit their borders.
In short, the vanilla game isn’t that good, it has some bugs but more annoying features in its campaign.
This game becomes more enjoyable if you use a mod.
I highly recommend DarthMod Empire which completely revamps the game, especially its campaign.
Making other nations less demanding and its battle AI a lot smarter.
Instead of marching into a meat grinder it tries to flank your meat grinder.

If you're a fan of otome or VNs then there is no excuse for you to not at least try Cinderella Phenomenon. From it's non-existent price tag, wonderful characters, beautiful art and excellent story telling, this game is everything a good VN should be.
CP takes those familiar fairy tales that we all know and love and gives them a little twist, making them the curses that plague the Lucette and the romanceable men. It's not done in a gimmicky way and never feels forced, it makes CP a breath of fresh air in a market when it still seems like a lot of otome/VNs are focused on slice-of-life, which isn't bad it just isn't new.
The biggest thing that stands out to me in the this game and makes it memorable though is the MC herself. I was fully prepared to either spend the entire game hating Lucette or just uninstalling it and forgetting it after spending a few moments with her in the beginning. She isn't a person I would like to even be in the same room with. Lucette is rude, selfish, tactless, untrusting, and doesn't have a kind bone in her body, but as you slowly find out why she is this way, it makes sense. I quickly grew to love her and cheer for her as she went on her Cinderella journey to accomplish three good deeds. Lucette is flawed, and that's what makes her perfect. She grows throughout the whole story on every single route, and it's made even more believable since the game takes place over months instead of days. The relationships and character growth actually have a time line that make sense.
The romance options are all different and wonderful as well. They all have the same basic conflict at their core, but each story is diverse so you never feel as though you're playing the same route over and over again. My only complaint lies with Fritz's route as it almost felt as though he was....forgotten? I don't know if it was just me but I felt like we saw less of his story and more of another character, however it was still a well-written route.
All the side characters are excellent as well, both the heroes and the villians. Everyone has a motivation for what they are doing, revenge, loyalty, love, greed, and all the characters feel full of life. I can easily say I loved all of them, even the villians.
Now, the only problem I had with the game itself might have been a RenPy issues more than anything. There were a few times that the game would simply crash on me or it would freeze while transitioning to the next scene. I also had a few times where I couldn't use the skip feature despite having just finished that route, and also could not use the fast forward button in the prologue of the game. They were quick issues to fix and I was able to avoid some of them once I found what they were.
That aside Cinderella Phenomenon is certainly a game that I will still love years from now and I look forward to anything else that Dicesuke produces. Like I said before, if you are a fan of this genre, there is no reason for you to at least not give this game a chance.

Ok my initial review panned this game.
Now I have figured out that it is EXACTLY like the campaign mode of the skirmish games Mordheim and Necromunda, and should be played EXACTLY like those.
Think XCOM 2 hardcore mode.  Take no risks.
I freaking love it.
Pros:
It's pretty-ish. Not great, not awful.
The involvement is as detailed as the tabletop rules for Necromunda
A lot of thought has gone into the mechanics of combat.
At no stage do you face a warband weaker than yours - Or Stronger.
Enemy warbands ALWAYS match you - even wounds appear on them
The 'develop your warband' aspect is great, but you're always short of cash.
Cons:
You're always short of cash until you max level.  Sitting there with 5 Warband members who can't learn skills or spells because you don't have the cash is infuriation incarnate.
You need to mob enemies to kill them...
But you also need someone not in combat to go and scavenge so you can have enough gold to pay your warband.
There are no difficulty levels.
So if this is a game you just want to sit down and play through the story for, forget it.  Every mission is a struggle.
There is no 'reload' mechanic, if your machine crashes, or the game bugs, you suffer massive hits to your entire warband, basically ending their career.
The AI is 'Special' - gets opponents stuck on terrain a lot, targets your DLC heroes over all others, makes odd attack choices.
Overall impression:
The satisfaction of walking away from a fight with no casualties due to careful tactics is wonderful.
Don't expect to have 'hero grunts'. Make your warriors fight as a team - they will last longer.
READ ALL THE SKILLS.  This game lends itself to specific builds for warriors. e.g. tank, crit machine, fear monger etc.
Specialists are more effective than generalists.
It is fun to personalize and build up your warband.
A very fun and entertaining turn based game, I got it on a sale but it is worth full price. They are adding new dlc at reasonable prices unlike the other big WH fantasy game thats out there.

This a really intriguing tactical game with good depth, many colorful classes featuring a myriad of skills, steeped in heady Warhammer lore and bearing moody graphics, which is unfortunately greatly marred by a horrid user interface that clips and hides text/figures and can even render certain story mission icons non visible in the majority of the resolutions chosen. The way in which deployments are handled: having to press A/D repeatedly to even place 1 unit properly is beyond tedious and there is no simple way to check the whole list of enchantments you have besides clicking on every enchantable slot.
However the most damning thing about the game is that it still bears many horrid random bugs that unfortunately render it unplayable for the luckless. One such bug involves a random "Round 1" freeze where the only way out of it is to abandon battle, thereby taking automatic injury rolls on all warband members, quite likely resulting in permadeath or permanent injuries. Yes, as there are no separate save/load files, such a bug effectively completely cripples a once promising warband through no fault of the player. To add insult to injury, after such a bug, you might also find your inventory completely emptied through some form of file corruption.
Another deadly bug involves a character getting stuck in a position in another character's zone of control whereby no actions may be taken and the game cannot proceed even if it's the player's turn. Once again the only choice is to abandon the battle and face the above penalties, which may well mean complete warband decimation and loss of many hours of play.
Of course there are also the numerous crashes to desktop and issues with Directx 11 and many many more and all of these issues are well documented in the bug subforums here. The issues I've highlighted barely even scratch the first page of said bug forum and there are literally 1.8k threads there.
There is the mark of a great game here and a persistent warband concept with hardcore leanings where mistakes are poorly tolerated and where it is fun to pick your battles/deployments well and to carefully manage your way to the top. But unless you don't mind seeing literally everything taken away in an instant because the game decided to throw you a random bug, I would suggest trying other turn based games. I reserve the right to flip this review when all these issues have been fixed but seeing as it has been nearly a year since this game has been out and had a fairly long beta testing phase before that, I doubt the bugs and UI issues are going away anytime soon.

The art style if this game is fantastic and the gameplay is solid. I love the setting and the personalities of the characters, and the mowing down of enemies always felt very rewarding. I do recommend this game, however I must address some problems I have with it, one being the controls.
The controls are not perfect, they work but they are defnitely flawed. I am mainly talking about the weapon switching mechanic, as most of the time you need to swap to a more effective weapon in the middle of combat but things are always so frantic and you have little time to react before your health is completely down. I just wish there was a more efficient way to go about it.
Also I want to talk about the game's length and difficulty balance. This game is rather short, I beat it within a couple of friends within a few hours. I did buy it while it was on sale I suppose it was worth it, but the thought of buying it at full price for the length that it is doesn't seem completly worth. The game's difficulty balance is definitely flawed, as I felt like it spiked up pretty hard after the first few segments. It went from being enjoyingly challenging to frustratingly difficult, more or less.
There are only three bosses to defeat in the entire campaign and I must say that only the first one was kind of fun. The second boss was moderately challenging, but that final boss was the most infuriating thing. EVERYTHING was pretty fun until that final boss. Three phases, all really annoying and very unfair. It felt like all of the bosses had way too much health, and I feel like there could have been so much more and what was there felt poorly executed.
Overall, this a charming run'n'gun game with a very appealing artstyle, however its length and boss fights are on the underwhelming side. If you're interested, buy it while it's on sale.

Ninja Senki DX is awesome.
Even though I'm a big fan of the platforming genre, I frequently feel like the usual backtracking and searching for secrets thing in this kind of games somehow gets in the way of having fun. Here, you don't have to do any of that. Collecting coins is completely optional, and you don't have to focus on anything beside getting to the end of the level. The whole game relies on this aspect, it's really polished, and as minimalistic as it gets, while deliciously challenging.
Besides, the art and japanese folklore-based bestiary is lovely, and the button-mashing against bosses and graphic style add a quirky aspect to the game that makes it really refreshing.
The music's great too, and the game is pure bliss to speedrun.
I think everyone who likes platformers can try it out without hesitating a second.

Ninja Senki DX does a good job of recapturing the feel of an NES game. It certainly has a has a charming aesthetic. The pixel art is well drawn with bold outlines and a varied color pallet. The soundtrack is also well composed and fits the Japanese aesthetic, taking inspiration from the game’s NES roots. The controls are tight and responsive, which is important in a platformer of this difficulty. While the game can get quite hard, the difficulty is never excessive, aside from a few frustrating boss encounters. The mechanics are simple and the level design is, for the most part, fair. The game is definitely on the shorter side, clocking in at just 3 hours for me, but there is enough content for the price point and the enemy and coin completion bonuses add a level of replay value. All in all, Ninja Senki DX is a game I’d recommend to anyone looking to scratch that “NES hard” itch.

A sugar-coated clone of Fairway Solitaire (Pyramid Solitaire + power-ups). Be careful with sugar-- too much saccharine will make you sick.
This one is definitely on the sick side... It's hard as hell if you want to get perfects everywhere (I'm not sure it fits the audience targeted by the Christmas theme..?), power-ups are few and far between (it takes the entire game to finally unlock 3 undos across 4 stages (!), for instance, and 2 of the 5 power-ups you can buy are completely useless), difficulty is only based on the number of cards you have to remove (so basically if you get a lucky draw you'll end with 15 cards to spare, otherwise you'll have to use half of your power-ups), the story is a couple of text panels that are an excuse for a synopsis (don't even get me started with the lackluster 'ending'), and the game is full of bugs.
At least the two main bugs are creative: the stats panel that shows up after you finished a stage will tell you you finished the current day, even though you didn't. If you reach the end of the day, the last panel will tell you you finished the NEXT day. Wow wow, no hurry! The worst bug, though, happens at the same moment: at the end of the day (half-day, technically, so every 4th message), if you're not happy with your performance, you can choose to replay the last stage. But unlike the previous 3 stages, you don't immediately start it again-- you're pushed back to the village screen, at which point you have to click Start, then Cancel, and you can replay stage 4... Except... Except you lose all of the power-ups you used in your previous try on stage 4. Well, that was a nice bug thank you. I nearly had to restart a series of stages from scratch towards the end of the game because of that bug.
I finished the game and didn't absolutely hate it, but the lack of heart that was put into this game is directly opposed to the Christmas theme. So that's a thumb down from me. Better play Regency Solitaire or Zombie Solitaire, these are much better. Even Chef Solitaire is better than this...

-Solid, fun gameplay
-Polished Art Design and smooth 3D animations
-Music (soothing/uplifting winter-themed and catchy)
-Sound Design is very rewarding when matches are made/hand is won
-Relaxing (this is a no-stress game with no negative feedback in-game)
-RPG-like elements (levelling up, power-ups, bonuses, undo's etc)
-Two progress hubs to track your progress (a snow village and an advent calendar!)
-Save/Resume in-progress game sessions
-Fullscreen & windowed modes (I am playing in 4K)
-25-30 hours of initial gameplay
-Has a good vibe to it
-Very replayable
-Card pile is random (some ppl consider that bad)
When this title first released on Steam it was over-priced at 10USD/GBP; that's steep.  The price was recently lowered to 4.99USD/GBP and at that price this is a buy for anyone who loves card games.  For everyone else, this is a must-buy Casual game when it's on sale.
If you like Solitaire games with quality art design, good winter-themed music, with power-ups, and high replayability, I would encourage you to pick up this underrated gem!

As a sucker for musically oriented video games, Savant - Ascent captured my attention from the start.
After booting it up, there's pure silence at the main menu. Odd. Highly out of place. You'd expect some sort of title music in most of your games to give you a sense of what to expect, depending on the overall theme right on entry.
Press Start, and your're treated to - what essentially boils down to - a slide show of stills showing you the story of what has occurred that leads up to your adventure as you "ascend" the tower. Quite literal. While not the most engaging, it's highly effective in its presentation. The lack of animation here is actually something I appreciated. It was out of place, much like the lack of title music, but it gave me all I needed to understand and infer the plot.
Next thing you know, the game begins!
You're treated to a short tutorial explaining the basic functions: X or Left Trigger to grab CD pieces, Right Stick to shoot your glowies of color, Left Stick to dodge. Simplistic.
The only thing is, you will die.
If you manage to continue at your base from New Game, I applaud you. But you WILL die. It's actually necessary that you do... If you've been collecting those CD pieces. They act as both your BGM and as your Power Up.
DUAL FUNCTIONALITY!
Each CD amounts to four pieces that you get from specific mechanized enemies that give off a yellow/goldish sheen. Take them out, and the piece is yours; you can get up to six CDs, each one adding a different mechanic that is NECESSARY to your progression.
After death, you begin again at the section that you left off, rather than starting back at the beginning. If you pause, you may choose to restart your section if need be. (FYI: It becomes handy, and almost needed, to begin at the beginning when you get your 5th Power Up and a certain "stone".)
For each CD you collect, you get a different musical style to accompany you. Most of it falls under the general genre of "Dubstep" and "Electro" - two of which I'm familiar with. While I don't like Dubstep too much, it adds to the retro-style look of the game with Chiptune themes and flourishes. The first four CDs are Dubstep, with the fifth being Drum & Bass. The sixth, at the time of writing, remains a mystery, but I hope it will be good!
Overall, after playing nearly two hours non-stop, it has been a great experience. Like I said, I'm a sucker for music games that have certain enemies or gameplay mechanics attached to a beat that require some strategy. This is more akin to a musical SHMUP - being on time doesn't particularly matter, but your mind will automatically sync up to it in some cases, which may hilariously lead to death.
Totally worth playing if you've got nothing else to do, or just feel like rocking out to some sweet jams.

I've been a fan of Aleksander Vinter for a while now, finding him when he was just staring his debut under his new alias, Savant, and I always had a soft spot for the music he produced. The chiptune-ish, 8-bit feel gave his music a kick that other songs never quite captured, and the overall melody and chord progression of his style was simply unmatched. So, like many, I was caught off guard when I learned that he was creating a game. After purchasing this and playing it for a while (I downloaded it onto my phone thanks to buying through Humble Bundle, and I racked up nearly ten hours alone on my phone version.), I have to say that this game is worth the price tag offered. Maybe even more. Not only do you get to hear several amazing tracks by Vinter, but you also get to experience a gorgeously made game with simplistic, but engaging, game mechanics. The difficulty progresses at a steady, but manageable, rate, and the rewards come easy enough that they would not cause frustration when trying to obtain them while still keeping the feel of difficulty and challenge.
Overall, for what went into the development of it, this game is worth the price tag and worth the time. I'd recommend to anyone who enjoys rail-like shooters with gorgeous graphics or those who enjoy simple, but addicting, games.

Vagante is awesome, I recommend it to anyone who is a fan of difficult roguelike games. This game is still in early access but there is enough content to warrant the early purchase. There are elements that still need to be improved but overall the core is very much there and extremely playable.
The controls are responsive, simple, and great on an Xbox gamepad. You can jump, melee, range, and cast magic at the press of a button; switching out weapons and magic is easy and fast with the swap button. Navigating through the inventory, magic book, and character sheet is also a breeze.
Alright now for the gameplay. You can expect to die a lot. Boulder traps, spikes, even gravity can bring you to a quick end. The walk button will become your best friend when exploring and keen observation will keep you alive. Another great element in this game is using the evironment to your advantage. Scouting the entire level for the perfect spot to vanquish a difficult boss can be very rewarding. Enemies are pretty generic but provide a fair and fun challenge, also the different approaches to triggering floor bosses is interesting whether it be a sleeping dragon or angry mother worm. Loot, glorious loot! You'll find all sorts of enchanted weapons, armor, scrolls, potions, and trinkets. Some items will drastically change up your strategy and even the way you travel.
This game is still in the development process and I'm very excited to see what the creators are going to add to Vagante. Changes I would like to see are variations on enemy and boss types ala the Binding of Isaac, being able to sell your loot to the shopkeeper, and more death screen statistics. It would also be cool to see what needs to be done to unlock the unlockables but as this game is still early stage it is understandable. I can't wait for the next update! Great job NukeNine team, I'm really looking forward to the finished game!

It's really the little things about Vagante that ruin it for me. At its core concept is a good idea for a game, whose elements are proven in other successful fun games, but unsatisfyingly combined in this one. It sits like some kind of fusion between Spelunky, Rogue's Legacy, and... well, the original Rogue. If Rogue were a 2D platformer, it be about this.
Unfortunately, I feel as if the game can't decide exactly what it wants to do. Spelunky chose to be, by and large, a puzzle game, where as Rogue's Legacy is far more of an action platformer. This is most evident in two factors: the kinds of traps and environments the games employ, and the damage systems they use.
Vagante takes a damage system more classically RPG. You have HP, and you deal damage to enemies based upon your attack power. Different kinds of enemies take different numbers of hit to defeat, This is a perfectly functional system on its own, suitable for a more action oriented Rogue-like platformer (such as Rogue's Legacy) but the environments in Vagante suffer a number of complications.
1) Poor visibility. Everything seems just a little too small in my opinion, and the color palette is sort of bland and samey. These factors combine to make a game where it's sometimes easy to miss little things. You learn to cope, but it makes the difficulty curve that much steeper. There's just little reason for a game's graphics to making it harder. Further more, the fog of war effect that limits your vision of enemies to only areas visible from your current position can cause enemies to flicker in and out of sight in a way that humans have evolved to find particularly distracting.
2) Bosses. A great idea to add to games like this, the bosses are very interesting to fight, save for the fact that somewhat clunky controls make it extremely difficult to come out with much HP. The real problem with bosses in my mind comes in with the addition of...
3) Instant death traps. A fine game mechanic as well, but as you vie for positions fighting bosses, it's all to easy to get tossed or knocked back or be forced to flee and find yourself instantly killed by some form of instant death trap. Have you ever noticed that platformers tend to put bosses into boxed off, isolated rooms? There's a game design reason for that besides memory. The action aspect of a boss battle combines very poorly with any form of instant death for landing on the wrong tile.
Ultimately, for a game that wants to feature fighting enemies, it sure chose to have slightly awkward controls. You can't run left or right while attacking, and you can't jump while in the attack animation. The most effective way to fight is to explore and  use the random environment to your advantage whenever you can, but as you knock enemies back and wait for them to jump back up toward you, you find yourself in an action game that constantly forces you to break its flow if you want to survive.
Flowbreaking aside, if the instant death traps vying for mental acuity with boss fights wasn't a problem and the controls were more polished, there's an issue of damage. Healing in the game is a bit TOO scarce. Ocassionally on some levels you can go almost unscathed, but on others you'll be lucky to leave barely alive, and when you're in the case of the latter, good luck having any chance of beating the following level.
All in all, this is yet again another 'rogue-like' game that's made itself more than 'difficult,' it's unreasonable.
P.S.
More of a nitpick than anything, but the item system in this game is more busywork than anything. Unless you get particularly good items, they're not so much better or different than anything else to make the system matter. It's kind of inherently frustrating though that classes favor different types of items, resulting in a bunch of stuff you find not interacting with your abilities.

I bought this little gem during the summer sale to use on a downstairs projector setup and I was dissapointed at first. However, after purchasing a set of powerline adapters I can connect the Steam Link directly to my PC through the power outlets in my house. There is literally no router between the Steam Link and my PC, just the adapters. I have experienced absolutely no lag or drop outs whatsoever with this direct connection. I also purchased a USB audio adapter to run audio to a sound system and it works flawlessly.
Before purchasing a Steam Link there are several things that should be considered. Are you relying soley on your wireless network? If you are I'd start with considering your wired options first. Will you be using powerline adapters? If you are, is your household wiring adequate enough? I'd say if your house was built or re-wired in the last 15 years you should be ok. Also, at least for me, I did not require a crossover cable with the adapters to direct connect to my PC.
The Steam Link, while not being a plug and play device from day one is incredible with the help from a few add ons. In the long run I've used it in several locations in my house with no hiccups and I am absolutely satisfied with it!

The pain makes the struggle worth while.
If you are a fan of Warhammer, or a fan of gritty fantasy in general this turn based immersive strategy game is for you.  You have control of each member of your Warband down to the color of his outfit.  Each unit has multiple paths, some less optimal than others, that they can progress through to work alongside each other.  The system uses a random number generator to plot out success or failure, but on the whole I have enjoyed my time with the game.  The teams are diverse enough in play style to make it worht a go at every faction and the ability to recruit select units as mercenaries from other factions only increaes the fun.  The injury and death system make the game even more worthwhile since you can never enter a battle haphazardly without the risk of losing those units you worked so hard on.  This element of consequence only adds to the flavor of the game in my opinion and is one of the best things about it. I strongly recommend this if you like games that reward and punish you for your choices.
Months Later and it still holds up for a great game.  With their Upcoming Necromunda adaptation I am sure I will be happy to purchase that as well.
