My Video Review:
Short summary:
TRI is an interesting puzzle game where you form triangles on walls to solve puzzles. The twist being that you'll eventually be able to walk on walls and redirect light and lasers with them. This is where I wholeheartedly recommended only half of TRI to some of you because while reflecting the lasers with your triangles sounds like a great idea on paper, in reality it can lead to a lot of pixel perfect placement that's more tedious than fun, especially in the later levels that revolve almost exclusively around this mechanic. Still, the mechanics and level design are pushed to their absolute creative limits here which lead to a lot of fun and intriguing "Aha!" moments.
TRI has a challenging difficulty curve that isn't afraid to present you with the seemingly impossible the further you play on. Also worth mentioning is the extremely appealing, simplistic artstyle and truly memorable soundtrack that accompanies this game. They really nailed TRI on the presentation side of things. A cute fox will follow you as you solve progressively harder puzzles while this light hearted chanting goes on in the background, and there's just something really enchanting and relaxing about that.
At it's best, TRI stands out strong in the puzzle genre right now. Even at it's worst, its still worth playing for any puzzler fan.

Empire total war is like a sickly child (no offence to anyone who might have one). Of course, it's your baby and you love it, but it's just not... there, you know?
Empire, even to this day, lacks polish (not the country, dangit) and there are still some absolutely ridiculous undertakings by the AI, most of which we'll get to later. But how about the pros and cons of the Vanilla game, shall we?
PROS
-excellent representation of 18th century warfare
-the emergence of nations, such as Greece, USA and Scotland (among others) is interesting and mixes the campaign up
-you may now contest in 3 theatres: America, India and Europe
-The campaign map is pretty, has lots of cool features such as towns that magically spring out of the ground, and a realistic intercept feature, meaning you can't just trot by an enemy army without implications
-Graphics are still ok, despite it's age
-Naval battles are a very welcome introduction, and they're pulled of qute well.
-Interesting tech tree
-Fantastic new trading system on the campaign map
CONS
-Battle AI can be gamebreaking
-AI diplomacy is all over the place
-Melee combat is an absolute snoozefest, and infantry charging is all sorts of broken, glitchy and weird
-18th century warfare means little in unique units within the same culture. All european armies will end up looking the same, just as all native american armies are just as similar
-With so much emphasis on the navy and trade, naval battles can become very frequent and very repetitive, especially in local trade theatres and against pirates
-Autoresolving is broken. You can have a 1500 army come up against 80 rebel swordmen and lose 300 men. How?
If you do get this game, i highly recommend DarthMod. I'm not gonna bother with the links etc. but it's definately worth a look see. The battles in Empire are underwhelming, especially with the poor AI, decision making and lack of bloodthirsty action, but DarthMod does a great job at reparing a few glaring problems as well as adding new features not only to battles, but the campaign as well.
The broken AI means i give this game an overall 6/10. The campaign map is the best it's ever been, but in battle, it's lackluster.
With DarthMod however, this bumbs it up to 8/10 level. Makes battles and campaign far more engaging.

I come from a console background only getting my first pc when i was 15, i'm now 17 pushing on 18 and for me i expect a certain standard for the games i play on pc none of the loot crate ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t i've come to expect. Alien Breed is a rather simple but fun isometric view shooter. The game is set aboard a spaceship and the single player campaign lasts around 8-9 hours. Although the game mainly involves walking through dark corridors and shooting at giant alien bugs, it manages to maintain a good sense of atmosphere. The player gets to use 5 different weapons, several items, and faces a healthy variety of enemies, which does well at minimizing what could potentially have been a repetitive game. The situations vary greatly at times you might face one or two bugs at a time, and then at other times a whole wave would just burst out from the walls and floor around you and force you to battle for your own survival. The fact that enemies could come from anywhere doorways, vents, floor creates a sense of tension and keeps the player on edge. The plot is in a comic-book-style cutscenes, most of the things you do don’t seem to have much relevance. For most of the time when outside battles you just go around the huge ship searching dead people and lockers for spare ammo and credits (in-game money) and activate various computer systems in order to gain access to the next area. It could feel repetitive at times, but the main focus of the game is escaping from the aliens, so I suppose it’s not much of an issue really. There is also a chance to upgrade your weapons to give yourself a bit of an edge in combat. Each weapon has 3 different upgrade options: rate of fire, reload time, and damage per shot. Thought you can only ever have 1 upgrade active at a time for each gun, so the player will have to do some decision making and choose an upgrade that they feel is most suitable. This also opens a slight possibility for replay value. Without giving spoilers, I also want to mention that I was a bit disappointed with the final boss of the game. Its attacks kept repeating themselves over and over in a very repetitive pattern. However, this is only a mere 10-15 minutes of an otherwise very engaging and well-polished game. It’s quite simple at its core, but the quality of the presentation that it delivers is very respectable. Now after having completed the game, there are two more parts that await me and it seems the plot is still building towards something. This is not really a stand alone game, but more like a chapter of a book or an episode of a TV show. So I am quite eager to try out the second and third instalments in the series and see where this goes. Lastly to mention, the game also offers a co-op mode, which is a laught at time, thought it doesnt have the story-mode to it.

This ones a weird one for me. I really enjoyed the game. I really did. But let me explain why it's weird.
The weird:
~Starting off is the price. I feel like 30eur (at the time of writing) is far too much given the age of the game. Combine that with DLC that isn't worth paying 1/4 of the asking price (8eur at the time of writing) makes this game a really "bad" deal. If you can find the deluxe edition for 10 or the base game for like 8 or so it is worth every single penny.
~Then we have the DLC. I felt like they weren't worth the purchase. Little content inside of them. Plain and simple.
~Now to free roaming. This game has a gorgeous city and setting. But when you finish the game it's all over. You have to start a previous mission if you want to roam around the city at all.
The good:
~Gunplay and game mechanics work well. No glaring omissions as far as I know.
~Graphics look slightly dated but are good and physx makes the game really visually pleasing (AMD gpu users need not apply because the cpu will get rekt, I tried).
~The game actually has many features that are missing from even the next game in the series, let alone modern games. Features include the ability to run out of gas and refuel, fixing a broken engine to keep going, hubcaps flying off of cars and quite a few more.
The bad:
~Drive here. Drive there. Drive back. It really gets repetitive. I don't mind pointless driving but here I noticed there was a lot of it.
~The story could use more missions. Or more content to the missions that already exist. There is a mission where you literally stand in the back of a truck and press E (or whatever the action button is) to throw 1 pack of cigarettes of the correct color for the customers.
Conclusion:
I would recommend playing this game. But you should really wait for a discount if you want to buy.

I dont write too many reviews unless the is incredibly bad or amazing. This game is the latter.. AMAZING. Mordheim takes the combat system of Valkyria: Chronicles, the unit customization of X-Com, psychology system of darkest dungeon, the unforgivability of an Ironman Mode and throws into a interesting story with an immersive atmosphere. As a note, I'm not a fan of 40k/warhammer etc. and have never played the tabletop.. Yet I love this game. I'd write more but I linked a video below that says it all.
TL;DR -
Pro's -
RPG progression
Great Combat System
Unit Movement is intuitive
In-game Currency/Management system is well balanced
PvP is intense
Real concequences
Good Story
Amazing Aestetics
Immersive atmosphere
Good Customization of Units
Cons -
AI is stupid
Steep Learning Curve
Ironman Mode
Continuous Autosave prevents you from taking back a mistake
There is a very steep learning curve which may put off the majority of casual players. I went through about 30 hours of loosing my entire warband (4 restarts) and having to start all over before I finally achieved a successful combination of soldiers. Of course once I learned the basics.. exploiting the AI became incredibly easy. 98% success rate on missions. Which leaves PvP for the challenge, and yes it is a challenge with real rewards and real consequences.
The Ironman mode you will find yourself in is Unforgiving. If your character gets critically hit (your standard high dmg crit in any game) he will suffer a permanent injury. By permanent injury, I mean he will loose an eye and have -10% chance to hit for the rest of the game, or loose an arm and never be able to dual wield or use a 2hander. He could loose a leg and never be able to climb again (Which is really important in this game). You will find yourself becoming the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ company man and firing any worker who gets hurt lol.
The movement system is amazing, just like in valkyria chronicles. You will recieve strategy points which can be used for certain types of active skills (Parry stance, climb, leap, jump down, etc.) or for movement. Each character has it's own movement radius based on his agility stats and gear equiped. Movement itself consumes 1 point giving you a radius to within, moving past the radius consumes another strategy point automatically. Early in the game you will have 4-6 strategy points while fully leveled up characters will have 7-12 points. Didnt get to the position you wanted this turn? Simply run back through your waypoints and get your Strategy points refunded.
The combat system is amazing

Tri is an underated puzzle game with a fantastically unique premise but sadly deserves a lot more attention than it is currently getting.
The games main puzzle concept relies on the use of these triangles you make called tri's. Initially these triangles have restricted use and can only be used to climb up walls. As you progress you unlock new uses for tri's. These include climbing up the sides of walls and reflecting light beams. These tri's are used to tackle every puzzle in the game.
Each level is set in a large freely explorable area. Your goal is to find three red lion statues in order to order the portal to progress to the next level. Completing various puzzles around the level will help you find your way towards these statues. Each puzzle is unique in it's own way, some involving uses of other things such as boxes, buttons or light. Each has it's own unique challenge that can prove quite diffcult.
What's even better about tri though is the way in which they create puzzles means they don't all have a single explicitly chosen solution. You can tackle many puzzles in your own unique way. Some puzzles will have only one solution possible but I found the majority to have multiple ways of doing. This personally adds highly to the user experience by not being restricted unnecessarily.
Puzzle progression in tri works almost perfectly. I could feel the difficulty rising as I progressed through levels but it was never too quick that I couldn't keep up. Earlier levels in the game I could finish in less than 15 minutes but later levels ended up taking me in excess of 1 hour to complete.
Now the reason I say the puzzle progression isn't perfect is because I believe they use the wrong premise to make the last 2 chapters the most difficult. These levels rely heavily on the reflecting light mechanic. The problem is that places tri's in the correct way to reflect light into the area you want it to is notoriously difficult. It's to the point that I almost gave up on the last 2 chapters. But I perseveared and the last chapter ended up taking me over 2 hours to complete because of this. I think the developers made the wrong choose to focus on this mechanic and it will leave a lot of people giving up out of anger.
Achievement hunters will love tri too. Each level has these extra secret findables called idols. To find these is entirely optional but they unlock you bonus content at the main menu. Sometimes they are hidden in obvious places such as behind some stairs or in a small whole in the wall. But more often then not they require some create puzzling to get to. Through my playthrough I didn't manage to find many of these idols and I tried to look for them in every nook and cranny I saw. So I believe these are very difficult to find and would be great to keep people occupied throughout the game.
Tri has a good amount of content contained in it. There are 15 chapters in this game. Overall it took me almost 20 hours to finish the game. This is a good amount of time and content. I believe you could finish it quicker if you were better at puzzles than me though! If you were looking to collect each idol as well I believe this could easily add in excess of 10 hours of playtime to the game.
In terms of graphic style it is very unique and stylish. Tri is one of the most colourful games I have seen in a while. They really do focus on making sure each area is as colourful and unique as possible which I applaude to. The screenshots of the game is personally what caught my attention to buy it. Along with this great graphics style is an excellent soundtrack. It is full of calming music to accompany you through your journey and captures the spirit of the game perfectly.
The story in the game is forgettable at best. Tri's story is told through after level cutscenes and the occasional speaking in game. I couldn't remember any of the story for the life of me which isn't good for a game. It doesn't help either that the vocals are terribly voice acted in a voice that I suppose the person thought would be interesting and unique but is in fact incredibly annoying. Luckily though the gameplay makes up for the boring story.
Overall tri is a puzzle game that really does deserve a lot more attention than it is currently getting. It is almost on par with other great puzzle games such as talos principle and portal. The issues I have with this game are mostly negligable. The issue with the last 2 chapters however did put my overall rating down slightly cause it annoyed me a great deal. But for a price of £12.99 it is quite reasonable for the amount of great content you'll be getting.

I loved the concept of Among the Sleep.  How many games have you play through the eyes of a toddler? This is certainly the only one I am aware of.  I can give bonus points for originality here and in a horror title no less, which is no easy thing to do these days.
Among the Sleep does a terrific job at immersing you into the world because of its engrossing atmosphere and ambiance. I will admit I was pretty spooked at certain points.  The mechanics are reminiscent of Frictional Games' Amnesia and Penumbra titles; you can interact with items in the world but there is zero puzzle solving that you will find in the aforementioned games.  It is more so a matter of finding and interacting with objects that help you progress through the game.
You cannot fight the few enemies encountered, instead, you must avoid them at all costs and make your way past them.  This characteristic of horror games I have found is either absolutely loved or hated typically.  I personally enjoy it because it puts the player in a helpless state and gives you all the more reason to be scared.  This is, after all, the effect all horror games should invoke.  But there are those who are annoyed or frustrated by this and I can understand that.
Among the Sleep unfortunately suffers from a few issues however.  My biggest problem with it is the technical issues I have experienced.  The amount of stuttering I encountered was surprisingly bothersome.  Considering the very short length of the game (anywhere between 1 and 4 hours depending on your playstyle and if you are hunting for achievements), you would have expected it to be significantly more polished.  The stuttering and major fps drops are distracting and certainly take away from game's immersion.  I could have 150 fps for a moment then suddenly it drops just below 60 and it is awfully noticeable.  My rig also is running on an 6600k, gtx 980, and 16 gb of ram, way above the game's recommended requirements.
The last but smaller problem I had with the game is the save system.  Throughout each chapter, as you play, the game will notify you that it's saving which is all well and good if you die because you will restart from your last save point.  Unfortunately though, if you quit a chapter mid game, you will have to start that chapter from the very beginning.  Not a huge deal given its short length but misleading because when you see the game autosaving, you assume you can just quit and return at the moment of the auto save, not the case here.
All this aside, Among the Sleep is a unique experience and is definitely worth adding to your library.  I would suggest waiting for a nice sale to pick it up though.

Yatagarasu Attack on Cataclysm is a successor to an older project simply called Yatagarasu. Its more of an update to that than a sequel in all honesty and that is okay.
I backed this when it was having it's crowdfunding attempt and paying the bare minimum to get the game I did not expect future content beyond the alpha and was pleasantly surprised to be wrong.
The game itself is fun. It is a six button fighting game like some Capcom and similiar titles, but at heart it is more SNK feeling and considering it is a game from former SNK devs it is no surprise.
The 6 buttons consist of two punches, two kicks, and two parry buttons for high and low.
Right out of the gate there is one thing I really do not like about the game, but I will say that is just an issue I have with fighting games in general and that aside it is a solid game worth getting.
My issue with the parry buttons is mostly not liking button based parry mechanics in general and making it two whole buttons continues to bother me. All of the characters are well designed and fun, but they are mostly very basic. Besides a typical grappler, shoto, and so on they make little effort to innovate, but others are a bit more unique and even the ones who are not are chaming in their own right. Kotaro especially proved to be my favourite of the cast for this reason. Speaking of charming one of the more unique is the announcer system. Immediately after you pick a character you are expected to pick an announcer(or not if you are boring) from a selection of various Japanese and FGC figures or even the characters themeselves which is weird and funny to do and I enjoy it. You can even pick the mood of them between standard "peaceful" and "unlimited" which does not seem to hold too much of a difference but will get different lines from your preferred announcer at times.
The community is sadly not very active to my knowledge these days, but they are there and the game itself is still a good fighting game. The DLC might be a bit overpriced($30 for a couple of voices is insane) but its all extra stuff. None of the key content was cut from the game to make the DLC and the game itself is small, but very well made. Another recommended good fighting game for Steam!

Lighthearted Quake
Penguin arena was somewhat of a pleasant surprise, as I was expecting some simple indie game.
There is minimal story to the game. Basically, global warming has made it difficult for penguins to gether enough resources to survive. A godess arrives and states that only one tribe can survive and the others will have to pass away for the greater good. IN order to decide which tribe survives, the penguins battle it out on the remaining icebergs...
Gameplay revolves simple FPS mechanics and sliding. Each match sets you up as one of the tribes of penguins and you basically have to push the other tribes off the iceberg without being pushed off yourself. There are basically three game modes which are team (16 players/bots), duel (each tribe has one player and multiple lives) and unlimited ammo duel (like duel except you have unlimited ammo for weapons). You can play these modes against three/two/one team depending on your preferences. You start off with a basic snowball as a weapon, but you can find other weapons such as rapid fire fish, bombs and mines. Every time someone gets hit, they will be pushed back and slide all over the place (due to the slippery surface). this makes gameplay surprisingly fun and challenging (if somewhat unpredictable) as players will be sliding all over the place (which is similar to quake/UT where characters bounce arond after being shot). After falling off the iceberg, you take control of one of your surviving team members (if they are a bot). After all memebrs are dead you will become an immovable ghost towering above the arena, where you can launch explosives at the guuys below. Multiplayer is dead, but you can still play against bots.
There isn't much audio to the game. Weapons sound decent as well as the music. There is no voice acting.
Graphics are appealing. Everything looks cartoony which adds to a light hearted atmosphere. The penguin models look alright, but I keep being reminded of 'Firbies' (the toy) when ever I look at them (due to their short nature and beak).
If you want a cartoony and simplified quake-like game, this game has you covered.

Played almost all Resident Evil's to date. Honestly i was expecting to be put off by the radical ''FPS'' change. My expectations were not met. Welcome to the family.

Gameplay :
Resident Evil has not been this good since 4 . While it's still quite different to the original RE games , 7 still feels like the classics . This is by far the creepiest and most Horror like Resident Evil game yet . 7 takes you back to the series survival horror roots and you will want to conserve everything you have very carefully , I even found myself having to do this on Easy mode .
The atmosphere is on point throughout the game , accompanied by great music , and you're always looking over your shoulder wondering what's next . In classic Resident Evil style ,  there are a number of puzzles / item searches throughout the game , and while they can be confusing , they're not frustrating , there was no point were I was struggling or feeling like I wasn't enjoying the game , as challenging as some parts were .
Graphics :
This game looks amazing , it has all the modern graphics settings , plus a resolution scaling option that can make the game look even better , providing your PC can handle it .  there is major attention to detail  also .
The PC version feels unoptimized and needs some fixing though ,  as I did experience frame drops on a number of occasions , at one point near the garage I experienced lag so bad that I had to restart my game . My PC is very capable of handing this game , and I know other people have had similar issues .
For those wondering about the Anti Aliasing options , I found FXAA + TAA gave me the best results personally .
Conclusion :
Resident Evil 7 is what the series has badly needed since 4 , brilliant story , amazing music , spook horror atmosphere . It also has a bunch of extra content  , some that ties in with the main story . Veteran RE / Horror fans can also try the " Madhouse Mode " difficulty once they beeat the game ;) .  Resident Evil 7 has made the series great again and is one of the best horror games I have played in a long time , highly recommended !

My thoughts on this game is mixed. It's a fun game and every tenth level the bad guy comes with a time machine with his fake Caesar, which is a reward for going through the levels. The plot of the game is really simple, Jesus is trying to be killed by some athiest nerd from the future who has made sixty traps to kill Jesus. The nerd from the future also has made a fake Caesar who makes the roman soilders that appear theough out the game want to fight you. Also, Caesar is potrayed as a murderous pyscopath often thinking stuff like "Kill Jesus!" or "Kill! Kill! KILL!". The athiest nerd doesn't have terrible voice acting and when he talks you don't here any white noise, his quotes are really good, my favorite being "Why does it even mater to you if you save Jesus? He dies any way." I can't tell if the game is poorly made religous propaganda, an elongated physics test, or just a basic puzzle test  but what ever it is, it works.
The objective is pretty simple: solve a puzzle, use your ball to make one or two Roman soilders die, hopefully get a few stars while doing so, and don't kill Jesus and occasionally one of his friends. The levels start out extremely easy, taking seconds to complete, and a three star victory is almost always ensured and a retry feels like an insult to you. Near the middle of the game levels can be beaten in ten to fifteen seconds, every now and then you'll get two stars but comprihending the puzzles isn't a challange and retrys start to become more frequent but you only kind of feel bad when you mess up. But at the end, the game starts to get frustratingly difficult and it requires you to set up specfic situations for a victory, insuring a three star victory begins to require even more specific situations, levels begin to take over twenty seconds to beat, and re-dos become more and more frequent. But the annoyness of some parts of the game is erased when you kill Jesus with a fat cow falling at one hundred miles an hour.
If you want to get into puzzle games or if you haven't played anything that complex in a while, play this game. It's not a bad game and I would suggest buying it. And even if you do get bored with the game then you can definitly find intresting ways to toture Jesus, or you could work towards getting one of the achievements like "Hell bound" which requires you to kill Jesus fifty times or the achivment "Zealot" which gives you the long task of killing one hundred fifty Romans, which you definitly can't get from playing the first level on repeat for ten straight minutes. My rating for this game is 6/10.

Particularly when a leader with an 89% hit is beat 1 on 1 by a henchman because of hit rate. Granted that only happened once but you can see the annoyance level.The "random" number generator that governs hits seems to favor high numbers, I noticed that the numbers coming up for hits, ran over 70 very often this is probable but inlikely, which leads me to conclude that it needs adjustment.

Its not like my warband would just pack up and leave because they beat the enemy, Warbands are there to gather resources and fulfill missions. quite often there is a bed of warpstone and I route the enemy and can not get it as game ends.
Overall good , enjoyable, tactical game. That needs tweeking and added content.

If you don't want to read: 9/10 Turn-based Strategy; challenging, not punishing; multiplayer somewhat lacking.
Longer version:
The few Cons:
Multiplayer is seriously sub-optimal for playing against strangers. Matches are hard to find, partially because there is no automatic search-function going that would find an opponent of the same strength for you, partially because one does not see if there are games to be had without staying on a screen that has that as the only function, and partially because when one creates a game one can't see if someone else makes a game you would be ready to accept.
If you want Multiplayer, get 1-3 friends to challenge.
Story Mode is short and minimal, and compensates by being absolutely brutal. However, normal missions are the bread and butter, story missions just the cheese&ham, so it is not all that much of a con. And Story Missions are not required at all, beyond for gaining few points to make life easier (see below).
The game has the strategy common sin of being very hard for new players. However, there are mechanics in place for making starting all over easier the more one has played, and recovery within a save is quite possible. After some time, the difficulty, story missions aside, averages to medium-hard-easy: your starting troops are unreliable, in the middle the enemy may surprise you with better stuff than they began with, and at the end your experienced troops should not get easily overwhelmed. Half a con, if I may.
Now for the good stuff:
The game is quite balanced and has immense tactical depth.
Micromanaging is possible and as deep as one wants it to be, but not required beyond the minimum awareness.
The artstyle is good, while obviously not quite the same quality as AAA games. Few of us play TBS for absurdly good graphics, however, and it is beyond good enough.
Single Player, despite being short on story, is varied and good enough for (looks at time played), at least 450+ hours. AI is a bit dump, however.
This point can't pressed hard enough: Despite being a game made with a skeleton crew, the Devs are active on the forums and actually answer to constructive feedback beyond any and all call of duty. Nothing feels like having actual personal dialog with the devs, possibly multiple times a week.
Bug reports are read and acted upon. Feedback is routinely checked. We get information about what is going to happen and often why.
So as said: 9/10, bought this and both DLC:s, bought to two friends as presents and have 2 more copies to spare.
PS. Do, by the way, buy the DLC:s. Cheapish, good, not gamebreaking, and makes the very start somewhat easier.

I'm an Amiga veteran, going back to the release of the predecessors of this game, Alien Breed from 1991 and AB Special Edition '92, and of course the sucessors AB2, AB2 Tower Assault.
I bought this because I thought it massively cool that Team 17 was back in action (though the old crew has moved on to different endavours), and because I wanted to see how well the game had been carried 20 years into the future.
Initially, its seemed a nice change from the typical shooters, and you recognize both the straight-edged level layouts, as well as the cartoon-assisted story telling from the originals. 3D graphics, advanced effects, advanced audio etc. are of course new additions, which help a bit.
What doesn't help is that the level design has you do a fair bit of back tracking, plus some of the ways to move through the levels are simplynot clearly visible until you've put a good deal of level scenery under close scrutiny, after which you'll moan in exasperation because it was otherwise (somewhat)-obvious what you should have done, yet you spent hours figuring it out. The ingame mapping function doesn't really help, because on the map, doorways are indistinguishable from regular bulkheads between adjacent rooms.
The alien "shock" effects get old and boring very quickly, and the game ends up feeling like a regular shooter with you hosing down the walls with lead in short order. Meh.
Lastly, the control system is a study in frustration, and that the dev team went with the system they did is deserving of criticism. I lost count of how often I accidentally turned instead of sidestepping, which may be due to me being keyboard handicapped, but still. It's not easy to learn, and its no fun at all being unable to properly control your character in the heat of battle because of mistaken keypresses. That, and the repeated inability to move in a certain direction because you haven't properly cleared a piece of debris, blocking your path, or because theres an actual, but barely visible, ALIEN IN THE WAY!
I'll recommend that you *don't* buy this, with two exceptions:
* You VERY much want to relive Alien Breed like I did.
* The game is steeply discounted from its regular price (think 75%+ price reduction).
It saddens me to not recommend it by default, but oh well, times change.
(Org. written 22feb2015)
Update: There is a particular sequence of events on the second level where the keyboard control needs to be near-perfect to survive, and where you are not given the aid from the game of any autosave checkpoints. Having tried to do this several times, where minor imperfections in placement and keyboard control means certain death, this underscores the problems of isometric perspective gaming combined with wierd and occasionally problematic keyboard controls. I came very close to uninstalling the game entirely at that point, but kept on till I suceeded through pure persistence. Stuff like this is not only not entertaining, but it is not at all a worthy use of your time.
Update 2 (26feb2015): Having finished the game (after an unintuitive end boss fight that I had to chickenshit out of by reading how to do it....) I can say that while the controls become comfortable after a while of learning them and thus removes an element of frustration from the game, the games repetitiveness in both combat and level objectives becomes more apparent. The game ending is essentially absent, it is merely an advertisement to buy the sequel.
Summarised: This games controls are unwieldy and takes time to lean before you can play the game properly and not be terribly inconvenienced (or dead), the action is repetitive and gets boring quickly, the weapons are not much different from each other (flamethrower excepted), the weapon&items upgrades system is seemingly useless, the non-action aspects of the gameplay is likewise repetitive, there is no depth to the whole experience, and the ending is a disappointment. The comic-strip storytelling, the occasional pretty backdrops and likewise occasional shock change in environments helps a bit, but simply cannot save this game from its shortcomings.
I have yet to try Co-op, and imagine that it can only help this failure of a game.
I will still carry on and see how AB:Assault is, out of sheer tenacity... or masochism. I don't know.

I had the most fun when there were more open areas with many different aliens running around, then it felt like a good shooter. I avoided Alien Breed: Impact for a long time. This was mainly due to the hum drum demo and the fact that Valve's team (at the time) had released Alien Swarm for free. But (as is always the way) I got this game free in a humble bundle at some point. And as luck would have it, this week, I was in the mood for some alien-shooting adventures!
First up, the tone at the start of the game left me feeling unsure about things, with those weird comic-art-with-voiceover-on-top, bits. But, this quickly changed once I picked up a nice weapon and started performing my character's engineer tasks. And...once I started kicking bottom, too! Honestly, I enjoyed this game. There's very little to complain about, overall. However, as always, let me get some downers out of the way first...
It's too easy on Veteran (Normal) mode. Although there were some challenging rooms along the way, I probably died around 3-5 times overall. Two of which, were down to me dying from a gas filled room that I hadn't realised was killing my character! It's also worth mentioning that I killed the final boss on the first go, with very little effort! So, yeah, it's fun, but, too easy. Which, as you might imagine, means that there's not much challenge. Perhaps the next difficulty up, would be adviseable?? Oh, btw, the ending is very...abrupt. It felt like those old shareware games that teased the next episode. So, I didn't feel hugely accomplished once I'd beaten the game :P
As I mentioned earlier, I wasn't totally sold on the comic bits at the beginning of each level. These fill in the story, but It felt like they cut corners here. They could've had simple in-engine cutscenes that would've fit, better. Still, that's just my opinion. Maybe they were going for a comic book type look at this point. Oh, and, your character is a little dismissive and arrogant towards your "friend," throughout. I remember saying out loud at one point, "you're a bit of a♥♥♥♥♥♥ aren't you?"
Apart from that, I enjoyed what Alien Breed had to offer. There were a nice amount of weapons, decent action, a nice amount of enemy types to keep things interesting, and I enjoyed exploring the ship to see what I could find. It almost felt a teeny-tiny little bit Metroidvania. But only a tiny bit. I liked having to look for medkits, ammo and finding logs, etc. That gave it a little more substance.
Overall, I give Alien Breed a thumbs-up!

That's right, this is a thumbs up.  Now I'm not recommending that anyone actually
for this game.  That would be a very silly thing to do.  But if you are among the thousands who already own the game from a bundle or a giveaway, I do recommend that you give it a shot.  It can be fun, as long as you are aware of the following:
- This isn't a flight sim, it's a rail shooter.  There is no freedom of movement, other than dodging enemy planes & projectiles
- You use arrow keys to dodge, the mouse to shoot, B to replenish missiles (usually not available), and R in conjunction with the arrow keys to barrel roll.  Yes, you have to use your third hand for this last one.
- Don't lead enemies with your fire.  It doesn't work.  Only shoot when the reticle is on top of them, and the shots will magically hit.
- The graphics are at most servicable.  You can edit autoexec.lua in the install directory to change the resolution from the default 1280x720, but that doesn't improve things much.
- The times that the "powerups" are granted make no sense.  You can get autofire in between enemy waves, armor repair seconds into a level, 7 levels in a row with no extra lives and then suddenly 3 in one level.
- Once you lose all your lives, it's Game Over, start over from level 1.
- Unless playing on Easy (which I didn't try), choose the "middle" plane.  The heavy one is a sitting duck that blocks your vision as much as it blocks enemy fire.  The light one dies if a boss as much as looks at it.
- A not insignificant amount of damage you take will be from enemies colliding with you from behind.  This includes helicopters that somehow overtake your state of the art jet fighter while moving backwards.  To minimize the occurance of this, try not to spend a lot of time at the top of of the available dodge area.
So, um, yeah, that's all that's needed to somehow enjoy the game.  At least it was enough for me.

Don't bother with this, not even for a buck. I got this in bundle like ages ago and even then I feel ripped off.
So, the game is a rail shooter and looks outdated as all hell. I knew that going in and was okay with it. And then you actually play it. First of all there is no manual, no control settings, nothing. It's not just that you can't rebind the keys, you can't even look them up in game. I had to check a guide to know the basic controls, because they are not intuitive at all. So you aim with the mouse, shoot with the lef mouse button, aim rockets with the right one and use the booster with the middle (wheel). Okay, so far so good. You have limited control over the plane with the cursor keys (no, not WASD and no, you cannot rebind them), which is necessary to be able to dodge some and keep enemies in focus. However, there's also B and R. B buys rockets (one by one until you hit an unspecified limit where you can't get more) and R does a barrel roll (you can't do that with the heavy plane), which essential for survival. Except, you have your right hand on the mouse, your left on the cursor keys, so good luck actually reaching R and B without getting killed.
If you manage to stomach the controls, the game still has more issues for you to cope with. The graphics are not just♥♥♥♥♥♥ they are low res (800 x 600) and forced to fullscreen. Oh, and all the water you see on the official screenshots? It's not actually there. As in the water texture is literally missing, so every ship looks like as if they were floating in air. Considering that out of the first 10 missions 9 plays over some body of water, this is quite a major garphical issue.
As for the actual gameplay, the normal enemies are the same throughout the game and kinda boring. They are dangerous only because the rail you are locked on makes no sense, especially on the later stages. Your plane moves erratically, hardly ever keeping the actual enemy planes in sight for more than a couple of seconds. Occasionally enemies come from behind you, crashing into you (taking away health) or you get shot by rockets from impossible to dodge angles because of this and there's not much you can do against that. Now, if you do combos (as in kill a lot of enemies in a row) you get bonuses: 4-5 gets you laser sight (useless), about 7-8 resets the overheat on your main gun, 9-11 sets in autofire (kinda useless, though autofire doesn't overheat your weapon for some reason), about 13 gives you a pack of rockets and I think about 15 gives you a life. This would be cool, if it wasn't literally impossible to reach the higher combos on most levels. See, the game ususally throws groups of 3-5 at you, very ocdcasionally 2 groups of 3-5 from different angels. Once you shoot these down, there's a 2-3 seconds break before the next group. This break is not enough for the weapon overheat to reset, but more than enough for your combo counter to reset. And, no, you cannot wait for the next group to show up before you shoot down the first one, because then the first group is likely to spam the screen full of rockets, costing you a lot of health.
The bosses look kinda cool (the only graphically acceptable part of the game really), but essentially all of them work the same way: they are big, tanky and essentially stationary with your plane flying in a predefined loop around them. Now bosses have gun placements that you can serparately take out to disarm them, except hitting the turrets do little to no damage to the boss itself and each turret has like a third of the health of the boss. And every boss have like 6-10 turrets. In other words, it's suicide to go for the tuurrets, just unload on the main body of the boss. The bosses will inevitably kill you, as the rail is just stupid. Like the stage 10 boss have a whole array of forward facing lasers that cannot shoot sideways or backwards. So if you were to control the plane, you would probably approach from the sides or from behind where the boss is only light defended with a couple of machine guns, right? How is the rail set up? 2/3 of it is a full frontal attack with no space to dodge or cover to hide behind. I did my best to move around, had the booster on all the time and still lost my last two lives there. Oh, and mind youm this was on easy. I seriously don't think the game is actually beatable on hard, and very doubtful about medium.
Oh, that reminds me: the game has no save system. If you run out of health, you get a new plane immediately. If you run out of lives, you will have to restart the game from the beginning. And since the game is VERY unfair with nonsensical rails to shoot from, you will die a lot even on easy.
So, yeah, this game isn't just overly simplistic and bad looking, but downright horrible to actually play.

TRI is a first-person puzzle like The Talos Principle or Portal. This game consists of unique puzzle solving and exploration,mostly for secrets.
The main mechanic of this game is building triangles. Just select three points in a certain area to create a triangle to make your own plattforms to reach new stuff. New mechanics are added to this later like
.
There is a background story which is being told with the cut scenes between the levels or the narrator which leads you through the levels at some points.
My main problems with this game are the jumping at times and how the levels seem to drag on a bit too long if you want to collect the collectables which are very well hidden at times. If you don't care about stuff like that then the pacing of the game might feel better.

I orignally purchased the regular edition because I've always found all that bonus stuff to be nothing but superfluous, unsubstantial fluff, but then I played the game... and heard the soundtrack. And holy hell what an amazing soundtrack it is, so I got the deluxe edition. TRI is the only game I've done this with.
Listen here:
As for the game itself, TRI is a very stylized puzzle-platformer sporting some amazing architecture; a combination oriental vibes and colourful minimalism. You solve puzzles by creating triangles to use as platforms, and as you progress, you gain the ability to walk on these triangles on vertical surfaces, and reflect light off of them. In lieu of this is a story about two gods, a pair of foxes, parting ways for reasons that becomes clearer as you progress. And to aid you with that progress is a mysterious monk.
Gameplay is solid, puzzles go from easy to challening, the voice acting is really good. Overall, you're looking at a quality product, so if you're into first-person puzzlers you can't go wrong with Tri: Of Friendship and Madness.

Penguins Arena: Sedna's World is an indie arena based game. You take the role of a penguin, your goal: knock the other team's penguins into the shark infested water.
There is no gore or voice communication within the game, thus making it a safe purchase for your young one. It's a cutesy game that can actually be a lot of fun.
There are three modes:
Teams (Classic): Your goal is to knock the other penguin teams into the shark filled water. You'll have AI teammates who fight alongside you. Each team will start with 6 lives, if played with two teams.
Duels: Similar to "Teams (Classic)" your goal is to knock the other teams into the water and negate all of their lives. Instead of having teammates within your team, you're fighting the other teams penguin representative of a sort. There will only be three AIs and yourself on the battlegrounds if you're fighting with four teams. Different results for other amounts of teams.
Unlimited: This mode is pretty much chaos. You're granted an unlimited number of an item that you pick up. Does not apply to the Sedna's Egg item.
Now, each of these modes allow you to change the difficulty via a slider as well as add the amount of teams you'd like to face. There can be a total of four teams at a time.
This game does support lan as well as web multiplayer. I have not been able to find matches for either. I am somewhat disappointed, however, I find the single player mode to be sufficient enough.
What are the gameplay mechanics for this game? They're listed below.
Snowball - Mouse 1 Attack, long range snowball attack. This will knockback players in the hopes that you'll knock them off the ice.
Punch - Mouse 2 Attack, melee style attack. This is used to punch penguins a very short distance.
Sedna's Egg - Gives you the protection of Sedna. - Makes you invulnerable to snowball knockbacks for a short period of time.
Dynamite Fish - A customized grenade. - An AOE grenade that inflicts knockback of all enemies within it's range.
Bear's Claws - Reduce the sliding effect.
Big Bomb - A powerful projectile. Replaces the snowball for one shot, inflicts major knockback to the enemy it hits.
Gust of Clownfishes - A projectile buff that allows you to shoot 10 clown fish at a rapid fire rate.
You are playing on ice, you're bound to slide around, especially when hit.
There isn't much to this game, the concept is the same throughout all three game modes. Although this game is very bland, it is definitely a fun little purchase. It's a bit pricey, especially if you just want the standalone game. This game is only sold in a pack for $15.00. Now, if you're in the mood to spend a little cash on a fun little game, and possibly a few others, this is worth your money.

I went into this thinking that I would have a separate section for each installment in this trilogy, but (after putting what I have deemed significant time into each of them) I have decided to lump them all in together as there wasn’t much difference between any of them. That being said, let’s get started shall we?
I – Story [2/10]
The gist of the story is this: Conrad, the Chief Engineer of the Leopold, are trying to restore power to your ship whilst doing battle with hordes of aliens and contending with a possessed AI. And that, kids, is all she wrote. I realize this is a remake, but honestly? That’s all?
II – UI [6/10]
In part one of the trilogy (Alien Breed: Impact) the UI (or User Interface for the less savvy among us) was colored blue and was infuriatingly hard to see at almost any given moment. Thankfully, in installments two and three, the color had been changed to green and was infinitely easier on the eyes. The mini-map was rather reliable, making it mostly unnecessary to consult the full map often. Apart from that, HUD was minimal and user friendly.
III – Gameplay [1/10]
Altogether I found Alien Breed to be underwhelming practically at every turn. The game is played from a top-down angle with rigid and irritating camera controls. The objectives were mind-numbingly repetitive and I found myself getting overly bored about an hour into the first game. I present to you a dramatization of just about every thing you do in these games.
“Turn on the cranky thing to put out the fires.”
*Kills aliens*
“Oh no, the cranky thing is broken. Go reboot six computers to fix the cranky thing.”
*Kills aliens*
“Good job on rebooting the computers. You can turn on the cranky thing now. Also, here are some more aliens for you to kill.”
And that, ladies and gentlemen, is quite seriously the entire game. Sure, you get an odd boss battle here and there, but I’ll be damned if they aren’t just as repetitive and underwhelming as the rest of the game. My other biggest complaint about all the games was the weapon upgrading system. This game is how far into the future and I can only have one upgrade installed on my weapon at a time? What kind of garbage is that?
IV – Content [4/10]
With this being a trilogy, you’d assume they’d add some new content into each game right? Well, they did, but I had you going there didn’t I? Impact was easily the worst game in the trilogy. The campaign (in all three games, mind you) was downright awful. Part two (Alien Breed: Assault) added in a “Survival Mode” which was mildly entertaining. It was a billion times more fun than the campaign, that’s for sure. The enemies felt uninspired; most of them looked like the bugs from Starship Troopers only fatter and more ludicrous. The weapons were a bit boring as well, though I did particularly enjoy using the flamethrower. (Who doesn’t?)
V – Visual [6/10]
There isn’t much to say here really. The graphics throughout the trilogy were consistently the same, with varying levels of obnoxious explosions everywhere. I realize the ship is crashing, but come on. That being said, the graphics weren’t too bad and the lighting was good.
VI – Audio [4/10]
I found the sound effects to be rather lacking. The guns weren’t thrilling in the least and the little, face-hugger-esque aliens, I would swear on my non-existant childrens’ graves’, were frog noises. Isometric sci-fi shooter. Fix that ship, blast them aliens. Gunfrenzy-facehugger-backtrackfest.
Your ship is wrecked and full of aliens. You have guns, an engineer’s degree and an android guide to tell you how to get things done. Test your cardio running all over the place blasting unwelcomed guests while enjoying the smooth animations, beautiful lightning, realistic effects and overall outstanding graphic design (with the exception of the GUI who sadly doesn't look as polished as the rest.)
For moments it feels like you're in there, trying desperately to avoid being killed by hordes of vicious aliens, thinking if that tin can of a ship won't give up on you before you can do something about it. Only one thing breaks the illusion: for some reason the camera can turn only on 45 degrees intervals, making it difficult to orient yourself and avoid being attacked by surprise.
With some good will and patience you can get used to it, but then you realize you're a space errand boy who's forced to backtrack every single time a task is completed, just to check if everything worked as it was supposed to. With time, that sensation grows and start to erode the fun. You start to wander... Who designed this ship? Surely someone not worried about time, who enjoys long walks and repetitive tasks. Like a puppy (or it was Intex?) Sod off Intex!
To sum up, with a more detailed and polished interface; and without so much walks up and down the same corridors this game would have turned out way better. The graphics and animations are great, the sound effects complete the illusion of being 'there' and the music rounds it up well. The plot is what it is and the repetitive nature of the story development kills the fun after an hour or two, but there are quite a few reasons to come back and play again and try your hand on different difficulty levels or even multiplayer.

Mafia II is a good game. At least I do think it is. The story-telling is good, the characters are well written, the atmosphere is top notch and perfectly renders the 40-50s universe 2K wanted us to live in. As for the gameplay, it's simple yet it works quite well (cover system, aiming are both pretty good). Finally, for a 2011 game, it doesnt look bad, even to this day. Of course, when you've played GTA V it might look a bit lackluster, still i enjoyed this game more.
Now, for the cons.. well Mafia isnt flawless, far from it. First of all, there are FAR too many bugs and crashes. Physx crashes your game (sometimes it even crashes for no apparent reason), AI sucks balls (and bugs out a lot) and many others (from simple visual glitches to gamebreaking character floating in the air, preventing any interaction with the environnement).
The driving's very hard to master and to be honest, i did not enjoy it. It's kinda random.
I also do not think the game needed to be open-world, as it adds literally nothing. You wont spend time exploring it, since there's nothing to see, nor anything to do. So in the end, it's a con for me.
I've seen a lot of people comparing this game to gta. Well to my mind, even if it looks very similar, both game shouldnt have had the same goal (open world gangster stuff), and i think 2k could have done better (a longer game, more focused on a few areas and not on an empty open world).
Now i still had a lot of fun. I really took a keen interest for Vito, as i could identify to the character since he was so human. Which doesnt happen very often. The atmosphere was really really good and I've been sucked into 2k's world until the end, so yes, it is a good game. However not flawless.

I found this to be an OK game. Concept of being a toddler was new and interesting. The rest was mostly old news. The scare factor comes mostly from 2 things for most of the game: loud random bg noise, giving the impression you are not alone; and scripted jumpscares. While I thoroughly enjoyed the 1st factor, the 2nd one became boring really fast, to the point where I wouldn’t feel threatened at all. The addition of enemies (which felt mostly scripted too) solved that issue in a way, at least for me.
First off: SAVING MECHANICS LIE TO YOU. You see all those dandy “saving” notifications in the bottom right corner? Yes, they are saving checkpoints. For when you *die*. If you close the game mid chapter and reload, you’re forced to repeat the whole chapter. It isn’t fun, especially on longer chapters where you might want to take a break, and where the checkpoint system makes it look like you’ll be dropped where you left off.
Graphics were ok. Some strange clipping if you actually pay attention but nothing too major. You can use the demo to check them for yourself, I barely noticed a difference.
NPCs push you out of the way (which is awkward when the main NPC is so small). Detection for the “climb up” command is really awkward in the last chapter where you have to walk into slightly higher places, not tall enough to be climbable, but I was unable to simply walk towards the 5cm higher place and get on it. That whole chapter had weird collision to think of it. I couldn’t get under furniture that I could get under in previous chapters.
Sound was nice and scary. A bit overdone, sometimes?
There wasn’t much to the story but then again you’re a toddler, your life isn’t expected to be super complicated anyway. It made sense in the end, wasn’t terrible or anything, but also isn’t going to stick with me.
Overall it was interesting. Not one of my favourite games, probably won’t go back to it after getting the achievements. Would still recommend checking out.

This, is what I define as a "Hidden Gem". By 8th Jan 2016, the game only received 150+ reviews on the store page, which is far from a satisfactory number compared to its excellence. What a Pity.
The game, TRI: Of Friendship and Madness, is possibly the best First Person Puzzler I have played in 5 years (since Portal 2). Of course, as to artistic merit (which is clearly not the main focus of this game anyway), this game falls far behind titles like Talos Principle or Antichamber. However, when it comes to gameplay, especially level design, this game is definitely among the best ones in the category.
Like every other hidden gems, this game is flawed, every outstanding aspect of the game, is accompanied by something not properly done which I'll break into details in the following paragraphs. Nonetheless, as I always believe, with flaws come the personality and sincerity, which are the criterions I used to define good works.
The core mechanism and most puzzles are cleverly designed, both logically and aesthetically. It's a rare one in the First Person Puzzler category that really nailed the 3D thinking, I mean, seriously into a 6DOF level. Let's take a look back, a sad fact is that a large portion of puzzles in other First Person Puzzlers can be easily recreated in a 2D format. (Yes, I'm specifically referring to the base game of Talos Principle here) But not in this game, the refreshing experience you would have when walking upside-down on the ceiling, is as inspiring as Portal provided years ago.
While the core mechanism gives you a large degree of freedom, it can also be easily exploited and overused. In more than one circumstance，I accidentally broke the puzzle with some tricky/cheaty methods, which I'm pretty sure is not the intended way. It might be welcomed by some players, but I personally do not like it. It's as if I broke the game along with its immersion and gaming context, which makes me feel retar*ed,  especially after I discovered the legit way to solve it later on.
Levels (after the first few ones) are huge and imaginative, full of secrets and alternative paths, the most important of all: WITHOUT ANY NAVIGATION ( or maybe a minimum amount of). This might sounds like a downside for modern gamers, but undoubtedly a diamond for nostalgic gamers like me. The game has all kinds of surprise in full stock waiting for you here and there , which simply gives you a sense of adventure and exploration, in your full control, unlike any other roller coaster experiences modern games would provide. It's hard not to relate this game to those old school classic FPS of the 90s with identical elements, such a sweet déjà vu.
Although I speak highly of its overall level design, the first few levels of the game are rather tedious and uninspiring, which I'm afraid is the major reason that prevented more people from knowing the game. But trust me, if you are patient enough to make it through the first quarter of the game, you will be amazed by how ambitious and imaginative the latter levels are.
Another thing worth mentioning is the soundtracks, which is definitely not the best but certainly among the most special tracks I have heard in video games. They are not those generic ambient/drone tracks you would normally expect in the puzzle game genre, but some world/tribal music instead. Some of them do also have an alienated context within that contributed greatly to the theme of the game.
But strangely, half the tracks end so suddenly with a harsh fadeout, almost feel like unfinished. And what's worse, is the vocal sound effects of the player controlled character, which is laughably bad. If by any luck the developers can read this, I seriously suggest you guys to take a second look on that. For it is, by far, the shortest plank of the game I can come up with.
So conclusively, if you're looking for an awe-inspiring experience and have enough patience and tolerance for those aformentioned flaws in the game, you would not regret to give it a try. Additionally, for achievement hunters out there like me, this is also a must-buy, for there is no grinding achievement at all but all gameplay boosters.

Empire Total War is probably the best colonial era game out there, following the Total War model, more realistic than Age of Empires 3 (in terms of formations, tactics, effectiveness of units) but not as hard to grasp as Cossacks (which has painful micromanagement and economy creating a steep learning curve) and with very nice graphics. It also is a pioneer with its naval combat system, granting a truely realistic feeling while still making logic and tactics prevail, and all this garnished with splendid graphics and damage, torn sails and broken masts accompanying the lively crew and hull damage to produce a dramatic effect.
ETW Brings the largest playable game map as of yet in any Total War Series, including many of the following titles, encompassing Europe, North Afrika, the Middle East and India, and Central and North America, bringing an immense diversity into the battlefields.
Unit Upgrades are also subtly but clearly visible in terms of effect, making technological research a key point in the player's strategy, ensuring that supperior units with advanced technology can make short work of hordes of low-tier units in a perfectly reasonable way.
Music is great, especially on the battlefield, accompanying epic and dramatic scenes with a grim and all too real lighting, scattered bodies and smoking ruins, making even a marching batallion look truly epic.
The only downsides are sometimes low framerate after quite some time in-game when there's more than a few smoking buildings, and irritating AI that persistently tries to steal technology and will raid everything in sight upon retreating, the AI however cannot be held against the game as it is reasonable, effective and not cheating.
On an aditional note, a full year after I wrote the initial review, I can say that playing with another nation is even more of a different experience than in the previous total war games, as geography seems to have a larger impact on your strategies now that you have three times the map you initially had, and terrain - unit combinations are many more than before.
Truly epic game, I recomend this to any history and Total War fan, it's easily a 9 out of 10!

Think The Sims, but with coffee shops. This is the me-ist game I've ever purchased. And yes, it's riddled with bugs, but that doesn't warrant bad reviews. (It really doesn't - I finished this game despite the bugs. There are cheat codes you can use to warp to the otherwise unreachable subsequent levels, and you'll find ways around the glitches. More on that later.) These bugs are definitely a shame, but I beg you to stick with it, or at least pick it up again when the patch rolls around. It is so worth playing.
The storyline is absurd. I love it. Gameplay is peppered with memes and mickey-taking, and it's worth taking the time to watch the cut scenes and read all the little tidbits of humour. The amount of work that went into this is just incredible - while the graphics aren't mindblowing (and I love that, to be honest), other aspects are laden with little details that make this game so fun.
Anyway - cheats. IDDQD was a life saver (warp to any level without losing your achievements) because during the cut scene at the end of the boardwalk level, one of the characters just gets stuck, and there appears to be no other way around it. In the mall level you must destroy drones to move on - well, these drones have a habit of turning invisible. As there's only one save file, saving the game with an invisible drone on the loose means you can't complete the level (unless you use the warp cheat). But I think the bug that causes this is pretty random, as I managed to surpass the level by saving the game every time I successfully killed a drone. If I got caught out by an invisible one, I simply quit and began from my last save point - and from then on, the drones never appeared at exactly the same time or place. It's a slow solution, but it works.
Believe me, this game will be better when the glitches are ironed out. I just want to defend it, though, because it is still absolutely hilarious and so enjoyable. The downtown level made me cry with laughter intermittently. Honestly, it's worth working through the glitches just to have Yasmar von Nodrog call you a donkey.

I want to start this review by stating that I love this game. It is fantastic. The fighting is fun and engaging, the deck system for building your style is fantastic and the way you learn moves is both hilarious and gives a sense of progression. The art style is stylized but minimalistic, and the added little graphics don’t get in the way of the fight.  It truly feels good to pull off the right combo to get around an attack and get yours in. Watching as you duck that punch and roll it into an uppercut is super satisfying, so is landing that combo finisher that almost always gets block. What I am trying to say, is that the core gameplay loop for this game is fantastic I just wish I could get more of it.
The crux of the matter her is that the game is primarily a PvP online game. Players are encouraged to play online all the time and have a rather smooth drop in drop out multiplayer coop experience in the open world. Players are also pushed towards queuing for online duels for better cosmetic loot and gear.
The online coop is fun, but presents its own challenges that can be frustrating on their own. Friendly fire is not turned off, and a slight misalignment of an attack can send that glorious spin kick into your buddies face instead of the enemy. It also opens the game up to some frustrating trolls. Players can and will knock you off ledges and send you falling to your death, forcing you to start some areas that have a bit of distance between check points over. It also means that getting ganked is a thing. But while frustrating that is part of the game and there is fun to be had in dancing around a troll as they try to get you to fall.
As for the 1v1 duels, they are best of 5 matches that are tense and engaging as you try and learn how your opponent fights and figure out how to best exploit the openings in his set, all while he is doing the same to you. Best of all you get some loot from winning the match and there is a solid basis of progression in the as you can learn moves from other players.
It’s a lot of fun. Now if only I could play online for more than an hour, if at all. As of right now the biggest issues with this game is its strongest point, the online play. Absolvers servers are almost always down it seems. While the game is still playable in an offline state it clearly missing something, and the single player “campaign” is only a few hours long, it is more of a tutorial than anything else. So, until the servers are more reliable I can’t really recommend this game. At least you find out rather fast if the servers are down, push button receive message about being unable to connect, turn game off. So until the servers are fix, I can’t fully recommend this game, hold off on getting it until that’s solved.
Edit: The server stability issues have been resolved. there still seems to be a bit of lag at times and some maches do lag out. but I can actually get online and stay online. Review chaged to recomended.

I followed Absolver for a long time -- remember all those E3 videos? -- and have played in the beta and release.  The game is amazing, with some caveats.
Yes, the servers are groaning under the load, and they are still fixing bugs.  However, Absolver is absolutely worth your time as it stands, mainly for its beautifully animated and meticulously crafted combat system -- a great foundation upon which I think they will build an amazing game with more content to come in the future.
The combat is just incredibly engaging -- it requires fast paced decision making, but the input options are simple, unlike some fighting games.  There is a huge element of crafting and customization in your combat deck, and accumulating new moves to experiment with is very satisfying.  The reward of creating a cool combination of moves is also in the visuals, generating strings of motion that both flow and have surprisingly accurate hitboxes.
Stylistically, the game is gorgeous, and very coherent in the look it maintains.  The world is beautifully put together, although the game is only about half the size of what you'd expect for a 3D adventure/exploration style game.
What gives me the most hope for the game is the developers.  They have been extremely communicative regarding player concerns (they communicate via Reddit, Discord, etc.), and they have outlined plans for a lot of free DLC content in the form of new modes, new PVE content, and new moves, weapons, and styles. The community has a lot of faith right now that fixes and more content are on the way, and I think sloclap can capitalize on that to build the game into something that will endure for a long time.

An on rails shooter in the vein of the old Star Fox or Panzer Dragoon games, but not nearly as good. There's a severe lack of feedback on anything you do in this game; your bullets don't actually make contact with enemies so much as your reticule damages them. You get extra lives, extra rockets, and gun overheating cool down powerups through out the levels at set points, but without any sort of warning, consistency or purpose. Should you use up all your rockets now? Overheat your gun for this wave of enemies? Maybe. Dodging enemy fire is a similarly mysterious affair of flying in a hopefully evasive square pattern.
On the other hand the gameplay is nostalgically evocative of older, better titles. The boss designs are pretty neat, though ultimately wasted on the game mechanics available. There is a framework for a classic arcade shooter here provided someone took the time to realize it. If you got this for pennies in some bundle, I can't wholeheartedly recommend neglecting it if you have any sort of fondness for the games it's poorly trying to emulate. Worth ten to twenty minutes of your time, but not much more.

I'm giving this game both a thumbs up and thumbs down. The reason why I'm choosing thumbs down as my official score though, is because of how horrid its multiplayer connection is. So TL;DR - if you're playing single player, you'll have some fun. But most people will be trying to get this game for coop since it's advertised as a coop game. And to them, I say: If you want couch coop, you should be fine. But online? Run away. Run far, far away.
That said, onto the bullet points.
+ Clean, crisp graphics
+ Fun and lively characters/enemies
+ Awesome 80's era imagery and dialogue
+ Relatively straightforward beat em up, can't really go wrong if that's what you're looking for
+ Varied power ups and abilities
+ IF YOU DON'T PLAY ONLINE, 2 player coop is what makes the game shine. Alot of mechanics (including high five power ups and "resurrecting" your "bro") open up.
+ If you're solo you can turn on a "bro bot".
+ Challenging. This isn't an easy game.
- ONLINE MULTIPLAYER IS BAD. At least, when it came to my experience. Stuttering lag, desyncing, disconnects every few minutes, crashes...everything you can think of, it happened. I bought this game for both myself and a friend, and I'm currently regretting it.
- Online latency can basically ruin Adobo fights and those that need you to dodge quickly. One of their main things is interrupting your combo with a hammer fist like attack. This attack gives just enough time and just enough of a tell to give you a chance to dodge out of the way. But online....nope. You will get hit. Every time. You're forced to use other tactics and so far I haven't found one that works well enough online. Of course, keep in mind my meager amount of hours in this game. I could just be showing off my newbieness.
- Battle mechanics are noticeably much different than the older Double Dragons.
- Running is....odd. Your character winds up and then starts running, which can lead to completely messing you up in all sorts of ways. There are certain mechanics that need you to run away or quickly get under some sort of cover. If you time it like you would any other game with running mechanics, prepare to find yourself on the floor.
- There is no grab and knee to face. Why did they not add this? That was a staple in many of the double dragon games. It feels as if a large chunk of the soul of double dragon was ripped out of it.
- enemies can juggle you pretty much indefinitely. I do love a challenge but it can get obnoxious, especially since enemies do a considerable amount of damage to you per hit.
- enemies are also invulnerable when they're swinging a weapon at you. So if you try to interrupt an enemy that's wielding a knife, prepare to get hit anyway, and watch 1/3rd of your life disappear in one hit.
So...yeah. I want to really really like this game and I guess if I play the rest of it solo, I probably will like it. But as stated in the beginning, the main reason why people are going to buy this game is due to the desire to play with friends. If it fails on that level, then the game fails almost completely in my eyes.
Play solo? Go for it. Play couch coop? Go for it (if you want two controllers you'll have to look up how to get that to work. Supposedly it only works with one controller by default). Play online? No. Nonononono. You can try. You might have a better time than I. But I can only go with my own experience, and that experience says...no.

Have been replaying the mission over and over again and this is the first time I finished mafia 2 in steam. The gameplay is somehow mediocre and that's a shame, because what I dig about Mafia II is its story and the way it's told. I love gangster movie such as the godfather, so watching the exploits of Vito and his best friend, Joe, as they go from job to job, party with the ladies, and using your thompson to blast out gangsters really feels like mafia and damn that was an enjoyable experience.

Story 7.5/10
A fun storyline that takes lots of inspiration from movies like goodfellas, godfather etc
all the classic ganster tropes are here led by our main character Vito. Vito is a cool cat though a little emotionless and dull at times. the game is rife with twists and turns that keep things interesting but dont expect Mafia 2 to go beyond the convensions of its genre. not every one you meet will be memerable but the games main cast is deep enough for you to stay engaged with the narative.
Graphics 9/10
Mafia 2 absoluety comes to life on PC. I remember playing this game on my ps3 and the difference is staggering. 1080p 60 fps with the settings cranked this game is gorgeous and almost holds up today. cars are beautifully rendered with lavishly detailed interiors and engine bays which look gorgeous as you drive through Empire Bay which itself is equally pretty. Every area of the city is varied and different and packed with detail. The lighting system is gorgeous and light sources cast shadows beautifully. The game has Physx technology which still impresses me in 2017. the way clothing bounces around dynamically based on your input is just straight up cool and something that should be more commonplace today. Cover is fully destructable in mafia 2 which looks ♥♥♥♥ing awesome and makes the games gunbattles even more immersive. Performance is good but i did encounter lots of random fps drops down to 30 fps for seemingly no reason. It only occured after the snow section and only lasts a few seconds before returning to 60. as pretty as this game is some of the less important character models can look very rough and lifeless even for 2011.
Gameplay 8.5/10
Mafia 2 is an open world 3rd person shooter with driving. The shooting in this game is pretty damn fun. guns have a nice feel to them and the sound is good as well. AI is just alright. The destrtuctable enviroments really add alot to the gun fights . It really feels badass walking up to an enemy behind cover while holding a tommy gun on your hip dumping clips as peices of wall and bullet casings fly all over the place. enemies will react dynamically to where you shoot them and will leave bullet wounds. I really love the driving in this game. Cars have a real weighty feel to them which i personally like especially when driving cars from this era. you are also able to change your rims, paint and upgrade your engine.
Polish 9/10
You can really feel the love put in this game. you can tell the amount of thought put into every layer of the game. i didn't encounter a single major glitch. This game really feels AAA
Overall score 8.6/10

The gameplay consists of your controlling a marine through 5 stages of corridors and rooms, searching for weapons such as Shotguns, Laser Rifles and the powerful Ion Spike, or items such as a Med Kit, Armor, Grenades, or the useful Sentry Gun which can be placed in specific power points in the maps. You will also find Intex Terminals, which will allow you to buy more ammo, sell unwanted items, and save your game.
A variety of aliens will burst from walls and the floor and attempt to EAT YOU as you move around the maps, so always be alert and watch your back. Things can get frantic and dangerous if your not careful.
I highly recommend this game! Even after completion, you may find it fun to keep playing to get better Leaderboard scores, or to help your friends get co op achievements.
