Okay, so I saw the trailers and watched a bit of the gameplay, which looks great so I thought I'd give it a try. And even though my ♥♥♥♥♥♥ toaster can't handle the game as well as I hoped it would, since graphics look beautiful but also a bit simplistic,  I still find Absolver to be absolutely amazing!
I had a frozen loading screen at one point and one crash (which is not uncommon for a new game) but other than that I had no I problems whatsoever. Me being in europe, I didn't have any problems with the servers which seems to be the case in other zones so I won't base my review on technical issues.
As I mentioned, the art style is very beautiful and if you saw the trailers I think you'd know that by now. What I really (really really) like about Absolver is that you can customize your own fighting style and it doesn't seem to really matter what level you are. The other players (until now) were all friendly as far as I could tell since there is no chat but only gestures you can use to express your... Eh... Feelings? Of course you sometimes end up in fights since the NPCs have limited moves and we all love challenges but since there is always "friendly fire" you might end up in fights by accident. If you lose fights, it's because either you or your deck sucks xD (in my case it was both). But as you fight the enemies (NPCs or other players) you notice, that it's important to observe their movements and react accordingly. One thing disturbes me though and it is that these guys, whose only purpose is to beat each other up, die from falling from like 4 meters height. Of course you'd take damage (in real life we might or might not break our legs)  but I still hope they change that.
All in all I think Absolver is not just a "smash-all-buttons-beat'em up-game" but so much more and if you like the trailers and the gameplay videos you should maybe just give it a try, that's how I did it (you might want to use a controller though).  Needless to say, my thumb is still hurting from me neglecting my real life tasks and it is still worth it.
I honestly think it's a great game, developers just need to add more features and actively work on it.
The bees knees, now we wait to see if the devs support the game.

This Game is absolutly amazing. It is by far THE BEST combat game I have ever played. The graphics are phenominal and super immersive, and the story is hidden from you in the begining, which is an awesome concept that leaves the player to find out the story on their own at various locations.
The school system is probably the highlight of the game. It enables people to teach new players how the game works, and show them different strategies, move sets, and the layout of the land. Super handy for new players!
A lot of games focus on raw combat, and players dominating others. The world of Absolver among players seems to be 95% of the time peacfull, players always willing to help and be coperative. The minute I came into the game for the first time in the multiplayer random encounter map. (Right after the tutorial) Some guy challenged me and I was like "Oh sh*t its going to be one of these games" But suprisingly, he showed me the basics of combat, stances, and all the other things that are not really specified in the tutorial.
Absolver is not really oriented for casual players, mostly because of how complex the controls are. Even so the game can be played casually and still be really fun.
The only issues I have had so far are servers being down at times, which is okay, because being a new game they might not have the capacity to hold all the player that want to play this awesome game
Overall, this game has my vote of approval. Fantastic job! Now im going to rack up some more hours.
Have fun enjoying Absolver!

I recommend this game for a particular reason. It is good! Very good as a matter of fact however, it is NOT Resident Evil.
I cannot stress this enough that if this is your first game you're playing as you dive into the Resident Evil Saga, please understand that this game (VII) in no way shape or form reflects the plot and/or theme of the original series. Unfortunatley at the end they name drop one of the main protagonist from the series (SPOILER) Chris Redfield and the big bad company behind everything Umbrella. Aside from that, I am going to get into a detailed review about Resident Evil VIII.
Let's look at the good, the bad and the wrong.
The good -
* Storyline (Stand alone game) is great! Really enjoyable however once you realize you're unable to develop a further understanding without purchasing DLC, well... That hurts.
* Gameplay is smooth, crisp and response time is very well done. There are times where the character feels a bit sluggish, but it needs to be remembered that this is a survival horror, not a FPS. Realistcally some actions take delay, which is why this is a + on the gameplay.
* Graphically - Holy SH*T. From shading, lighting and the interactive qualities of the enviroment. This is some premium work!
* Unforgiving - Leave it to Havok. Make sure, as you play, to conserve and prepare. I actually found myself on the final boss, out of ammo for my primary weapons, and was basillcay SOL. RE7 does make an effort to prepare you for the battle, but its up to you to explore and find obtain said equipment.
* Video Taps (SPOILER) - While immserive breaking, they're very cool in assisting players not waste precious resources by implementing an almost demo bit to attempt a certain area.
The bad -
* Tool Tips/Loading Tips. This will give you near literal itteration on how to defeat anything you're having problems with. Why? It takes the learning portion of our survival out of it.
* Document Control. Unlike other RE's, you're unable to store (at least copies) of the articles, lab reports, newarticles, etc. that you find through the game. Perhaps it isn't very important due to the Tool Tips tell you all the answers...and...
* Grocery Questing. This is a horrible implementation for any game. By looking at the map screen you can see all the things YOU need to do. Boring! This really defeats the limited open world aspect of RE. This limits the player to think on their own and develop a crutch on the mini-map rathat than their ability to navigate and solve puzzles.
The wrong
* DLC for Story? This is for real. Additional content, further plot and story understanding can only be found via the DLC. That's a real shame considering the game is $60. That leaves a real nasty taste in my mouth.
* NOT Resident Evil. As it goes, this game is more of a Rob Zombie flick. The story, for the most part, is really enjoyable, Due to it being Capcom and having a Reisdent Evil title, you'll continue to try and wrap your mind around how exactly it fits into the genre. It's almost like a Terminator-Time-Line inception. And I am here to tell you, it doesn't make sense. The characters are all new, the plot deviates from Reisdent Evil (more on this...)
* Boss Battles (SPOILER). These are kind of lack luster. Almost kind of easy, but the problem is, there are 3 primary residences, but we only fight Jack and Marguerete (SP). I didn't recall exactly if we fought the 'son.' The concepts behind the 3 boss FIGHTS are interesting, but they're more offensive mechanics rather than structures way to defeat them. Pretty much unload enough ammo onto anything and it should die at some point.
* Bugs, Molds, Pukers. Again, not a Resident Evil game that I familiar with. I am grateful for the minor boss mutations, but where are the zombies? lickers? Ivys? There was a perfect oppertunity in the game for them to introduce a familiar monster, but instead I am left pumping a countless amount of ammo into the boss.
* Immersion Breaking (SPOILER). Are these guys all outfitted with GoPros? And who is rendering their digital footage into VHS Low Def? Maybe that's what Lucas is spending all of his time doing at the end of the game?
OVERALL -
Solid game, shouldn't belong in the RE series unless it is reintroduced a stand alone portion. Great graphics, enjoyable story, always use a Headset, and turned up, at night. alone.

1. The game stutters like crazy. I tried various troubleshooting, but to no avail. My system is powerful enough to play pretty  much everything on high settings, but this game stutters. Seems like a really ♥♥♥♥♥♥ PC port.
2. The final boss requires grinding earlier stages to get upgrades. It's the only fight in the entire game that will give you trouble, other than maybe needing an extra shot at a couple stages. Basically, the final boss requires you to have upgraded a couple of your skills at shops on earlier levels. This kills the flow and creates a lot of unwanted padding in a game that should be a play-for-3-hours-and-forget kind of game.
While I like the game itself, these 2 issues are deal-breakers for me in terms of recommending the game. A crucial bad design choice, and a game that should be playable on any system having bad stuttering.

a story that plays and makes fun of the clichè (check the ending song for a better idea),
different action for each stage,
pleasant co-op,
with replay value for getting songs and all pwrups.
It's all mixed in a game that shows potential from the beginning.

Penguins Arena: Sedna's World is the kind of game that will almost instantly bring back memories to old school 90's gamers, and despite the fact that the game's appeal is as childish as it can be, that's what makes it even more interesting and nostalgic. There is no story here, Penguins Arena is pure arcade, and even though the days of minimalistic maps and limited abilities are long gone, this is the kind of game that still manages to keep you entertained for a while even in the absence of modern day game concepts. Getting into the game is easy, pressing only a few buttons in order to choose your preferred game mode and set the number of players, and after that you're pretty much good to go. The game's main attraction comes in the form of Teams mode, where up to each player takes control of an entire team of six penguins, allowing you to respawn if you die as long as you still have remaining penguins on your team. Aside from that you also have the Duels mode, where instead of having six penguins you only have one and the last one standing is the indisputable winner and the unlimited mode which is basically classic with an infinite number of penguins. All modes can be played against the AI, but the real fun comes in multiplayer where you can play against your friends or random people on the internet, and if you're really into bringing that 90's gaming feeling back entirely, the game can also be played using LAN Connection. As easy it is to set up games, as hard it is to control them; there's no option to switch the mode or map once you have started the match, so each time you have a sudden change of heart and want to replay a previous map in order to take revenge on your friends, you have to quit your current session and set up a new one, which can prove to be quite annoying, especially if you're doing this with friends and you want to spice up things a bit often.
Penguins Arena: Sedna's World's gameplay mechanics might not be the most refined or innovative out there, after all it's a game about penguins shooting snowballs at each other, and even that simple mechanic has problems working properly sometimes, but that barely bothered me at all. The point of the entire game is to eliminate the enemy penguins by pushing them outside the map; each snowball you land correctly will push your targeted enemy a bit backwards, leaving enemies standing on the edge of the map highly vulnerable. As for why would anyone stand on the edge of the map, well most of the maps are small, so standing in the center might not always be an option and also when you are engaging in four player multiplayer there will be more penguins surrounding you than you can count, so you will always get pushed around, making falling off the platform at some point inevitable. There's a cooldown of a few seconds for shooting snowballs, so pressing the left mouse button non-stop isn't the way to go here, so in theory calculating your throws and using power-ups wisely should ensure your victory; of course that isn't the case for most matches, as some explosions have questionable outcomes, lag will often make you miss shots that should have landed in the enemy penguin and the AI will prove to be more destructive than helpful, but even with all those issues the game still manages to be fun and make you want to take revenge on your friends in the next match instead of rage quitting and that pretty much describes 90's LAN Games magic unlike anything else. Power-ups are the biggest game changer and even though there are only four of them, making you wish that there were at least a few more to give the game a little bit more variety, those that are there have a significant impact on the game, with the Mine pushing enemies further than a snowball normally would, the dynamite fish that once placed down will explode and send anyone around it flying, the fish crate that changes your snowballs to more powerful fish for a few throws and the egg that makes you invulnerable to enemy attacks for a few seconds.
There is no good way to say this: as the game feels and plays like a 90s LAN arcade, it looks like one of those as well; the overall graphics are bad, but what is even worse is the repetition of environmental items, moving from one map to another is no big deal as they all look and feel the same and the only thing that differentiates one from another is the position of certain objects on that map. On top of that the number of maps available barely hits 10, as some of them feel way too similar one to another and playing for a few hours in 5 minutes matches will make it feel like they were repeating even faster. As for the visual effects, most of them are absent at all and the ones that are there look like everything else, brought back from a 90's - early 2000's PlayStation 2 game.
The sounds that the penguins make might seem funny and cute at first, but once you hear them over and over again they become boring, because quite frankly they're the same for every situation you'll ever come across. Audio effects are just as bad as the visuals, with sounds missing modern notions such as tonality or pitch, but just as any LAN Arcade game you will probably play this one with your music in the background; that is probably the best way to go since the soundtrack is just as annoying, with the same song playing over and over again until you eventually grow tired of it and stop noticing it at all.
Even with all the fun it proves to be once you get past the game's flaws, considering the small amount of maps and modes available, it is impossible not to get bored after a few hours and even though the game does have achievements for the hunters out there, those shouldn't take more than 3 hours to complete.
Let's be honest, Penguin's Arena: Sedna's World is not a good game, in fact it's a pretty bad one from every aspect, but it's fun and as long as you can find some friends to share that fun with you, this will prove to be a good investment in exchange for a few hours of arcade gaming.

Alrighty, let me start by saying my quarrels with the game. It is slow. It is unforgiving. It is not unfair like everyone who is writing a bad review says so.
It is slow in  how the battles unfold. Almost in a good way, because you do need to strategicly place your units and you have to crunch numbers on your risk/rewards. It is unforgiving in which to say YOU NEED MORE THAN YOUR TOP PLAYERS! It is almost like a rogue-like. Anything with permadeath and injuries should be taken that way. So train who you can, in all fields, or you won't easily be forgiven in being stingy.
Now here's the class session on how the numbers work, because the misunderstanding is giving a B average game a bad name.
-If I roll a d20, each numeral corresponding with 5% (1= 5%, 2=10%, 3=15%, etc.) with an 80% chance to Successfully SWING (Not hit) then all I need to do is roll a 4 or higher. Easy to hit right? No.
-Now the opponent rolls to see if the Successfully Dodge (granted I met the swing roll). Let's say they are in dodge stance for a 50% dodge rate. If you successfully swing, the opponent gets to check for an 11 roll or higher. If they do so successfully, tough♥♥♥♥♥♥ Thats how checks work.
-Normally in games like this a critical swing is only dodged by a critical roll as well, if at all.
So really, an 80% hit chance is a 40%. Or a 42ish% if critical swings bipass dodge rolls all together.
Anyways. My point is, don't buy into the "RNG is broken and unbalanced" ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t everyone is complaining about.

After playing this game for a very long time and producing Let's Plays for the Mercs, Sisters and Skaven Campaign (all available on YouTube under the same Nick) it is time to produce a review.
To start with the obvious: I gave this a thumbs up, otherwise I would not have spent so much time with it.
As with every game there are good and bad things and I am not trying to hide anything.
Let's start with the bad stuff:
AI: Above all the AI is the weakest part in the game. The AI will occasionally place impressive units (that cannot enter houses as they are too large) within a house and so making it completely useless unless you decide to run into that house and engage it. This is just one example of stupid things the AI does and while it has been improved it is still bad.
Pathing: The pathing has seen major improvements but it will still happen that you bump into every piece of furniture and that the AI runs into something and is not able to navigate it's way around the obstacle. Ambushes and Charges work better now and seem to only trigger if the target can be reached.
UI: The UI was designed with a console adaption in mind. For a game that has it's biggest fanbase (Warhammer ...) in the PC-faction this was a rather debateable move. Playing the game on a PC is by no means a problem but it is annoying that you somethimes have to click twice as often as it would be necessary. The UI has also been improved lately and some information is displayed (like ambush ranges), other information is still missing though (minimum range for ranged weapons, ...).
Now let's talk about the good stuff:
Customizing: Yeah, while I agree it can be better, we are at least not forced to run around with a bunch of cloned characters. This takes in mind both appearance and the skill build, it is totally possible to develop the same base unit into a ranged Critter or into a melee DD (that does not apply to all characters obviously).
Healthy Party-Refreshment: Alright I agree that is a bad title. Did not know what to call it though. For some this might be a negative thing but I love that your characters are actually at risk of dying while at the same time there are several steps in between from minor injuries to basically being a cripple with only 1 arm and a Peg Leg. In this area this game is even beating the game it is way to often compared too (XCom).
Tactics: The biggest plus side of the game! Due to the massive amount of skills that can produce synergy effects and the possibility to create bottle necks for ranged fighting or to instead spread out and look for as many 1on1s as possible this game has a huge versatility. This goes so far that for some warbands the choice of the map is more important as the choice of the difficulty.
This does by far not cover everything but should give you a nice overview what I think about the game.
I hope I was able to support your decision and in case you have any questions, just ask and I will gladly get back to you!
Cheers,
Chris

Long in the making, Attack on Cataclysm is finally here. Woohoo!
Okay, it's not quite perfect. It's clear that the developers put most of their effort into the gameplay itself, which boasts a really fun combat engine which falls somewhere between KoF 98 and Third Strike as far as combos, parrying and general movement go.
This is awesome, but then there's things like the overly convoluted, borderline ugly UI, slightly odd translation or expecting players to delve into their port settings to get it running correctly online. PC literate players will be fine, but more casual players may take a while to sort it all out. Oh, and there's a notable lack of configurable keybinding options and no resolution settings. Low res or no res, amigos.
That aside, it's pretty rad. I find the combat way more interesting than many of its contemporaries, given that so many fighters these days are sequels playing it safe, and despite living in the UK I've had some smooth matches so far - and that should improve once the GGPO update materializes.
Oh, and Aja's totally sweet. Glad she won the crowdfunding poll.
TL;DR - It's a genuinely great fighter so far lumbered with some awkward UI trappings.

Each character has a compact list of special moves so they are easy to learn and remember but because of the way YAoC has been designed, you'll be discovering a plethora of strategies and tidbits of knowledge for each fighter for weeks on end. Suddenly, a modest roster of 11 playable fighters becomes overwhelming (but promising). The reason this game is easy to learn and difficult to master is because it's been developed and handled with love by a tight group of former SNK developers which is famous for outstanding fighting games like King of Fighers, The Last Blade, and Samurai Showdown so you know you're getting into something made by people that know their stuff.

"Save Jesus" is a puzzle game with physical elements. Your job is to save THE Jesus Christ from Roman soldiers and a couple of other dangers by killing all soldiers and getting rid of traps that would send Jesus to heaven.
You do all that with several types of a ball (a rock with spikes, an inflated cow, a fire ball...), but all these types do the same thing so it's not like one ball is better than another.
You need to let this ball roll the right way and/or with the right timing while considering Jesus' safety and helpful items like explosive boxes that can move things around.
It's very simple and you can figure out the solutions yourself easily, at least in the first 30 or 40 levels. It can get challenging but not to a level that it'd get frustrating. It rather gets boring due to the rather dull and cheap-looking level and sound designs. Also the boss levels are actually like the regular ones, so they are not really exciting.
If you think "Well, Jesus is in it, so some comedy or controversy must be in it": No. He just silently stands around and is the only connection to the bible, it could be any character. This also goes for the Romans who just stand there and actually do nothing.
"Save Jesus" is a nice little time waster but nothing more. I'd say: Wait for a discount if you are really interested and don't pay too much for this. But it's not a must have. I don't regret trying it out but it reminds me of how little of these physical puzzle games there are like this on Steam and I wish for more and better ones.

I've only got 8 hours in, but I'm on island 4, and I've played a lot of the previous game.
The difficulty is ramped up in certain places, and the unlocks add to the replayability value. The people complaining about camp positions or waiting/traveling clearly have not played it past the first parts of the game. What is it about people today and instant gratification? If you want an easy game that you 'win' with no effort, play farmville or minecraft. Sure the beginning is rough, but by pushing through you are rewarded with unlocks and upgrades that make the base game easier while adding new elements to the game.
If the "ai is being stupid", you are not planning your moves correctly. I've yet to have the AI do something 'stupid' or unexpected, and I've been through several islands.
If camps are a far way away, you may have to lure them over several days. Sure, it'l set you behind a day or two, but once the chain gets moving the villagers will start flowing in. If you're really salty about the layout just re-start the map.
This is not a tower defense game, nor is it a casual zen game. It is a strategy game with deceptively simple controls. The strategy aspect is where you spend your money, and how. Money can be used to build up defenses, recruite new builders/archers/knights/etc, or be used to push back the greed (like when you are attacking a portal and your troops are out at night, preventing a battle). If you tell your builders to chop down trees, and you have a ton of other buildings queued up, don't be shocked when they run out of camp at night to chop the trees during a fight -- they are doing what you told them to do.
This game is extremely fun if you like strategy games and puzzles. My only negative is that they aren't charging more for this to fund an even bigger installment in this series.

It's a nice short and atmospheric game. Not worth 30 quid but if you're a horror fan, you can't go wrong with it when it's on sale.
The environments are creepy and the sound design is top-notch (although I can't figure out why the baby himself/herself sound like a monster themselves sometimes). There's isn't much in the way of puzzle solving or anything besides moving objects and pushing stuff around.
Graphics look gorgeous. The lighting is superb.
Be wary, though. There are clipping bugs galore; so don't be surprised if you get stuck on the environment occasionally and can't move. I had to restart a couple of levels because I got stuck in the ground and wound up where the game apparently didn't want me to be. Gameplay mechanics are pretty easy and I'm sure your non-gamer significant other can enjoy it as much as you do. Can't say it had much in the way of surprises or the story was that special but it did keep me interested throughout the 3-or-so hour experience. Sometimes I felt the developers had the atmosphere and story down but couldn't really come up with any new ideas for gameplay.
As I said earlier, if you find this on sale and you're into horror and toddling simulation, you'll get your bang out of Among the Sleep.

I just completed Among the Sleep. The game provides a disturbing couple of hours of gameplay. Definitely worth the buy. Just make sure your therapy is in order. It's a horror game with a 2-year old protaganist, so naturally there's fairly disturbing content and concepts in the game. I felt the designers did an excellent job of portraying the child-like perspective of the protaganist, and the locatons & settings were just theright mixture of creepy & surreal without ever going over the top.

I was pretty neutral but on the negative side of this game. First I didnt really find it scary at all, and I've always found myself to pretty susceptible to tht sort of thing. It really felt like the developers wanted you to play this game in VR cuz that deffinately would have added to it. Next the visuals were pretty shotty. I dont have the best computer, but things were clipping in and out of each other all the time. This made the game hard to get into. On the brighter side the atmosphere is great. The story is good too. Dispite issuses I had with the gameplay I found myself drawn to finish the story. Unlike a lot of other horror games where you have to go around and read everything in order to get the plot, this game doesnt do that. It does a good job with visual clues to help you figure everything out; building to the final reveal. The last negative would be the play time. I finished the game in just under four hours which was a little shorter than it should have been. There are a few collectables hidden thoughout the game to go back and look for, but seeing as how they arnt anything but incohesive crayon drawings there is no real reason.
Conclusion: at five bucks on sale it is hard to say no, but unless you can get this thing to work with a VR headset I say you might want to look around a bit more first

It has a very particular and well executed art style, which I super enjoy. The fighting system is fun. The AI is difficult, this game doesn't hold your hand. PvE is challenging, it's actually a good game in that regard. Yes you will have some fun with this game if you buy it. Still I can not recommend it for full price, wait until 50% off or some massive rebalancing. This game pretends to be a progression based rpg, while it's actually a simple fighting game.
It takes a massive grind to unlock moves. You're being forced to farm moves, which is very, very annoying. Even after playing through all the PvE content you haven't unlocked any significant amount of fighting moves. This forces you to play extremely dumb and stupid in npc fights, or getting slapped in the face a million times by a person. It honestly is no fun. Don't think that you'll be able to build your own fighter on your own, it's practically impossible. You'll find yourself grinding just because you bought the game... not because it's that special or so amazing that it'll take over the e-sport world.
PvP is massively unbalanced and super random (After all, nobody has the moves they want), so there it's a grind as well. And when you think, "hey that guy had a nice string of moves, I want that" ... you're♥♥♥♥♥♥out of luck. Good luck finding the npc that has the move and then evade and block until you get the move, which takes a couple of fights, because you also need to win. Rinse repeat for every single move in the game, which are more then a 100, and soon you'll find out that that's about the time it takes to grind.
Then you go and check out the 'school sytem', which is a 'social' thing, that allows people to make a deck of moves for others to use. Which sounds great in theory, but in practice you aren't actually getting the moves. You still need to unlock them, you're just able to play with them somehow. So if you want to change something... you can't. You are simply forced to use something you kinda have to, because there is no way to win otherwise; but also it isn't very satsfying because you can't adapt or change to the meta... so you're eternally stuck in that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t, until you eventually, you'll never guess this... grind to unlock all the moves yourself anyway.
There is no fast travel and the PvE world is 'open' for no reason other than to have you aimlessly run around. If you're♥♥♥♥♥♥with maps or directions, this game will frustrate you to no end. There are only a very few routes, so taking the wrong one is extremely time consuming. There is no minimap, the only map there is is extremely abstract and not actually very usable. The game uses instances and scales the number of enemies to however many people there are in the instance. This makes PvE unpredictable and running solo into 3 NPC's is not something you survive easily. Oh, but you can just run past everything, so actually who cares. There are only a few specific enemies you need to beat, in total there are like 10 PvE fights you need to actually win.
Tl;dr Do not buy if you enjoy character building, or actual fighting games, the grind to get moves is terrible and honestly not worth it. The PvE content is enjoyable, some fun can be had. Buy on a discount.

Absolver is an instance-based MMO where up to 4 players occupy the same region and fight NPCs or each other. The world map is big enough, but not huge by any means. The majority of the world consists of narrow pathways with few small openings allowing for combat. The features in this game are very seldomly explained to you.
There are four elements of progression:
(1) Prospect (General character levels)
(2) Combat Trial (PVP levels)
(3) School (Learning Abilities)
(4) Equipment
Overall, I find the game to be missing a bit of content for the $30 CAD pricepoint, but the combat complexity seems to make up for it. For fans of this genre, I think there's a lot of replayability.

I'm new to playing the Resident Evil franchise. It seems like I enjoyed the older games better. The newer games were action based and didn't really have anything "scary" or anything that gave you a feeling of hopelessness or despair as you hope nothing is around the corner.
Enter Resident Evil 7. I bought it to try it for two hours and I ended up getting hooked. From the beginning, the game keeps you on edge and gives exactly the feeling of dread I've been looking for. The lack of psych horror was very clear in the later RE games, but it seems 7 has hooked me.
As of this review, I have 36 hours played. I finished the story 3 times on normal and 1 on Madhouse. The game is difficult at times, but it makes it that much more rewarding when you finish off the boss fight or avoid getting gangbanged by three molded that cornered you at the end of the hallway.
I would recommend this game to anyone. Now I have to find another FP horror game to play, but I think not many of them will come close to the experience I had with RE 7.

Mordheim is a game for people who have played so many strategy / tactics games that they no longer feel the need to define themselves by how "hardcore" they are at playing games that simply hide just how much they coddle them behind layers of crunch.
Much like the Warhammer god Slaanesh is the god of (amongst other things) chasing more and more excess, Mordheim is a game for people who are utterly wracked by ennui at the prospect of grinding through another strategy / tactics game on hard mode that they really don't find very hard. No, the Mordheim buyer says, "Bad RNG rolls? Who cares! The more important question is, what happens when I fail them? Are the results hilarious?" If that sounds like you, Mordheim is the most definitely the game for you. (Especially the Chaos faction with its mutation mechanic.)
If you can't laugh at having hours of work invested in Your Dudes (or Dudettes in the case of the Sisters of Sigmar) wrecked by rolls on the injury chart at the end of battle that you only had to roll because you missed three consecutive "can't miss" hits in the last battle, there are plenty of other strategy and tactics games on Steam that will tell you you're the bestest commander in the world even though you can't handle your precious plans being upset by anything whatsoever.
There are two major flaws with the game as is. One, it's horribly optimized. I upgraded computers since purchasing it and it's still firmly in the "go make a sandwich while a map is loading" category of optimization. And two, it's kind of threadbare in content when it comes to factions and maps.

This game has a lot going for it.  It's a great turn-based strategy game with individual levelling for all characters.  There is a great feeling of satisfaction that goes into levelling up a party.  To that extent, it's a lot of fun, but it has some pretty serious issues.
This is a "hardcore" style game.  If a character gets hurt, he stays hurt.  If a character dies, he's gone forever.  this is an interesting dynamic which I typically do not like, but it's okay if it's done well.  In this game, it is done well.  Most of the time.  however, towards the end game, it turns into a game breaker, and I'll explain why.
The story missions are challenging, to say the least.  No, I'll go one step beyond that.  They are hard.
First of all, they put my warband into a tactically stupid situation that I would never put myself into.  Both of my archers were paired with my mage, and two of them were dead before they even had a turn on my first play-through.  On my second playthrough, after losing one of my archers to perma-death and firing the other because he was pretty much worthless after suffering a brain injury, I used only melee characters with much better success.  That doesn't change the fact that my warband was pretty much decimated due to a flaw in the game.  Oh well.  Another 20-30 hours of play time to get my warband powerful enough to take on the mission again.
On my second playthrough, I was plugging along just fine.  The basic premise behind that mission is that there is an invicincible opponent that goes around destroying all of your characters without batting an eye while the player struggles to figure out how to inflict damage on her.  When I finally figured out that you need to disable the pillars, it took three turns to arrive at the first pillar while this enemy is mercilessly killing my warband.  When I finally arrive, I think "finally.  I might be able to inflict some damage!"  But no.  I need some shard or something, and who knows where the heck that is.  Suddenly, it sinks in.  Even with the shard, it will take 5-6 turns to disable all of the pillars.  And that's not including the amount of time it will take to find the shard.  So, yeah.  My warband was completely decimated a second time, and I'm not willing to put 20-30 hours of play time into this game again just to get my warband powerful enough to take on the mission again.
Simply put, when I purchased this game, I was looking for two things.  I wanted a turn-based strategy game.  Check.  Secondly, I wanted a game where I had the ability to level up individual characters in my war party.  Check.  What I did not want is a puzzle game where if you get it wrong the first time, you realize you've wasted 20-30 hours of your life.  If I wanted to solve puzzles, I'd go play Portal.  There is a reason why I don't play Portal.  It's because I hate puzzle games.  What's worse than a puzzle game?  A puzzle game where failure is pretty much permanent.
If that type of frustration is what you are looking for in a game, then by all means:  Purchase Mordheim.  As it sits, this game took over 100 hours of my time, and I want that time back.

I'm just going to start by clarifying that I have not played any of the original Double Dragon games, so none of my opinions are going to be based off of comparing this game to the original games.
Let's start with what they got right. This game both looks and sounds awesome. The soundtrack is a joy to listen to and the visuals are very pleasing to the eye. However I can't recommend this game because of what it does wrong. The gameplay is difficult in the worst way possible, the totally unfair way. Whether it is unstoppable attacks or not landing a hit because you were just a smidge off on the vertical, this game is massively unfair. Now I've played frustratingly hard games before, but the ones I actually wound up enjoying were the ones that I felt gave me a fair shake in the game, and that when I messed up, it was 100% my fault. This game does not do that for me, and it does help that the controls are a mess. Everything controls slowly. You walk slow, you move vertically slow, and even the sprint is slow with it's half second to a second delay before you actually start running. Plus the duck isn't all that effective, and using it feels more like a roll of the dice to see if you get hit or not.
To me the biggest problem with this game is that it seems that the devs put more focus on the art and music than on the actual gameplay, and that they were looking to make a great looking game instead of a great playing game, which hurts it in my book. Part of me also feels that the devs thought that they could just make the game really good and not worry to much about the gameplay because people are going to like it anyways because it's a Double Dragon game. Because of this, I can't recommend this game.

Double Dragon: Neon is the latest installment in the long-running Double Dragon series. DD: Neon feels like a total reboot of the entire Double Dragon series, starting things over from scratch + then also taking it completely into its own direction. Paying homage to 1980's & 1990's culture in video games, movies, music, and so forth - DD:N succeeds in being an outlandish, ridiculous, funny, fun & often challenging brawler in the DD universe that especially fans of that era of brawlers should take on.
To begin with the basic DD premise, here's the story: Marion gets kidnapped by someone, so the Lee Brothers, Billy & Jimmy, head off & adventure out to find who took her, kick butt & go rescue her. That is just the start of things, as the game that feels grounded as it begins and then eventually adventures into outlandish + ridiculous over-the-top territory, not feeling like many of the older Double Dragon games. Neon is constantly tossing out 80's + 90's references and paying homage to the classic games, movies, music & things from that culture + era. This game is definitely not to be taken seriously - and thankfully, it fits b/c the game's just often really fun to actually play.
But, oh - can it also be challenging + frustrating, too. Multiple run-throughs of a level b/c of no auto-save placed in an entire level can be annoying + frustrating, feeling like a trip back to the 80's + 90's of difficult games from the Nintendo era. The game will save itself once you finish a level, though. So, you won't have to always restart from Level 1, if you need to leave the game + shut it off for a bit. And this all here was on its Normal difficulty (which is what you start with; you have to finish the game to unlock the others)!
Gameplay feels like your typical side-scrolling 2D-style brawler, for the most part. Of course, the game isn't without its own twists - by basically combining many classics brawlers + throwing some RPG upgrading-elements on top. If you've played classic fighters such as Streets of Rage series, Final Fight (some moves are just plain unrealistic + combat is faster than old Double Dragon) and especially Double Dragon (since it's still a bit methodical with its combat) - you basically know what you're getting into. Combat here just feels great with the X360 gamepad. While Neon is mostly a linear affair, like River City Ransom (NES), you may run into shops in-game where you can purchase upgrades for your skills + abilities. Constantly, you are defeating enemies + picking up power-ups for your skills (which are mixtapes + even have their own songs in the Inventory menu!).
If this all sounds good to you with gameplay + combat - well, you're in for a treat. Combat here is a lot of fun + a joy here to take part in, for the most part. Playing with the X360 controller, the controls felt very smooth + the game also ran very well, normally ranging from 55-60 frames per second on my PC (i7 950; 1 GB VRAM of GF GTX 560 Ti; 16 GB RAM; Win 7 64-bit) when set in a 1920x1080 resolution (1080p). The game sports a very nice artistic direction that just oozes cool for its 2D environments, while its 3D character models look also good. Don't expect a technical masterpiece here, this isn't Crysis - this game's all about its sweet art direction.
The music absolutely stands out here + sounds great, having that 80's & 90's vibe. Whether it's an actual song they made + performed with lyrics, or a piece that sounds like it could've been in an 80's movie, or a complete remix of a classic tune from Double Dragon games - the music always fits the bill and sounds great. No doubt about it, the soundtrack here is just always fantastic.
The game is not long, by any means per playthrough. For my first run-through, playing solo, it took around 4-5 hours approximately. There are Leaderboards, so you can compare your run-throughs & compete with other players online & even your Friends. Also, you can go through the Co-Op locally or on the Internet via Steam, so you can play with your Friends. Also, once unlocked - there are multiple difficulties, so if you want more of a Challenge and want to compete on the Leaderboards, it's certainly there. This all certainly could help the replay value, if you actually like the game & want to give it multiple run-throughs.
When it all comes down to it: DD:N is just a lot of fun, for the most part. It plays lots of homage to 80's + 90's culture, runs well, plays well, looks cool artistically, has a fantastic soundtrack & delivers a really solid experience. While auto-saves locations are placed after each level, some might like this challenge & feel that is reminiscant of games from an older era (Nintendo era). DD: Neon is quite good. Neon is often funny, outlandish, ridiculous, over-the-top & a flat-out fun brawler that gamers, especially fans of this genre (of brawlers), just should not miss.
Final Grade = B-.

Objectively speaking, this game isn't anything particularly new or special. But in reality, by my standards, it is the very definition of a hidden gem.
The gameplay is OK, not great - jumps are too floaty, and the combat is NES slow. That's not a compliment in this day and age. And some people probably feel that the Beat em Up genre is a bit dated too.
BUT. This game has some things definitely going for it.
1) The soundtrack might very well be the best soundtrack I've ever heard in a game. Period. It's that good. There's no weak tracks whatsoever. It's worth existing for this reason alone.
2) The game is hilarious, especially if you enjoy 80s culture. You level up with mixtapes, battle a dude who is clearly a Skeletor parody, get prompted to move forward when you linger too long by a Power Glove. My personal favorite moment is when you're in space, and have to fight outside the airlock holding your breath the whole time.
3) The gameplay is not bad at all, if you're playing co-op with a friend. There's nothing like going for a high five (gives you some of your pal's heath, if you're about to die) and then pulling a SIKE! and stealing all their health.
As of this writing, the game is available for a grand total of $1 if you go buy it at Indiegala. It's definitely worth it. Hit me up and I'll play it with you.

Excellent, fighting game with lots of depth well worth the price.  If you want a good fighter that is easy to pick up but hard to master and want to be part of a growing community this is an excellent game.
Pros:
* Old school fighting game with lots of depth and unique twists on systems from existing fight games.  High damage, flexibility in combos without being overly drawn out, and parries.
*Good network code (that will be improving even more in updates)
* Respectable cast of characters some similar to Street Fighter and some pretty unique in their own way.
* Already some pretty good resources (streamers/vids/forum posts) for tech on the game
* Beatiful sprite based artwork
* PC system requirements aren't demanding.
Cons:
* Like old school fighting games, single player is not where the longevity in the game lies.  Arcade/Story mode won't keep you busy for an extended period of time.
* UI is rough (but acceptable once you learn it especially for the price tag).
* Character trials are hidden in the training mode menu
* The beatiful 2D sprite based artwork doesn't allow for super high resolutions

If you've played one alien/monster/zombie/critter top down shooter you've played them all. This is virtually identical to Shadowgrounds, Alien Swarm, and that zombie one that I can't remember the name of right now. Yeah, they're terribly original.

You liked Alien Swarm? You'll like Alien Breed. You loved Dead Space? You'll probably like Alien Breed (because Isaac Clarke and Conrad are stranded in a spaceship, with few survivors and they're alone in that hell).
Alien Breed: Impact is apparently a reboot of an older game that I never played. Here, you're a member of a spaceship that found an old ship lost many many years ago. Well, found is perhaps soft as, if I remember correctly, you've collided with it. Anyway, Theo (aka you) has to survive in his ship, after loosing his family years ago, and has to trust a robot to guide him to the older ship. However, when weird creatures are appearing, Theo has to rely on guns and terminals to survive.
That's the solo campaign. You have a co-op campaign where you play with a friend as two other members of the ship and you're also trying to survive and to reach the older ship.
The game is seen in 3D isometric, meaning that you have a little time to adapt to the command and the view when you're used to 3rd person or 1st person game.
I remembered enjoy the game, mainly because you have perhaps normal weapons but also a powerful one, that I should add, different in each Alien Breed game. Yeah, true, when you're in the high difficulty, you have to adapt your way of playing before a game over because you didn't check your health.
Anyway, your PDA is also nice as you're finding also notes from other persons, you have also a nice map to see where you are... and the terminals are in reality a save point and a shop for ammo or health.
The HUD is blue, like the title in the header. So, everything (texts on the screen) will be blue too. The game is also told with cutscenes drawed as comics. And well, the blue is also the main color.
Alien Breed: Impact is a nice game, though I'm kinda sad in co-op, it was kinda lagging and that we lost each time at the end of the level. If you don't own the trilogy, you shouldn't hesitate!

4k graphics, blown away by the sound quality, the voice acting is superb. personally, one of my favorite quotes is "ya think yu can stop me? look it, ah gawt a tahme macheen!" very intricate and thought-out dialogue is one of this game's strongest points. in addition, the plot and lore of save jesus is so complex and designed so well that its almost like you are actually there in the game saving jesus! it is an experience similar to that of smoking weed, while dying and going to heaven but learning that jesus is in trouble so you save him and then wake up wondering... "what did i eat for dinner last night?" you look over to jesus in your bed and he stares back at you and then you wake up again to find that your entire existence was actually a dream in itself. anyway, every game has its downsides as well. save jesus is no exception. one of the worst parts about this game is the lack of an easy mode, as the difficulty rivals that of dark souls. another issue is the demanding system requirements. my macintosh computer at school has trouble running this game. constant crashes and it struggles to get even 10 fps. no problems on my *coughcough*superior*coughcough* pc though. in conclusion, save jesus is a fantastic AAA title that i recommend to any fans of the popular book series "the holy bible," based on this very game.  hope this review helps!
